title: design: external OAuth 2.0 / OIDC provider — third-party app integration via standard authorization-code flow
description:
## Why now

Cloudflare's 2026-06 "OAuth for All" announcement (https://blog.cloudflare.com/oauth-for-all/) opened OAuth delegation to any Worker — every developer on CF can now ship an OAuth-server surface. That raises a substrate-trust question for ART: should notme expose a CF-compatible OAuth dance so third-party apps that already speak OAuth (and may be deployed on CF) can use notme as their identity provider, the way they'd OAuth into Google / GitHub today?

## What's already shipped vs missing

notme's identity-bridge surface (per cloister.capnp `wellKnownIdentityBridge` route kind) already ships: `/.well-known/openid-configuration`, `/.well-known/jwks.json`, `/.well-known/webfinger`, `/.well-known/nostr.json`, `POST /oauth/token` (client_credentials grant).

Missing for a real third-party-app OAuth provider: `GET /oauth/authorize` (auth-code flow entrypoint), consent UI, apps registry (`client_id`/`client_secret`/`redirect_uri`), auth-code → token exchange on `/oauth/token`, PKCE (RFC 7636), token introspection (RFC 7662), revoke (RFC 7009), refresh-token grant.

## Decision matrix

A. **Wrap Ory Hydra as a sidecar** — battle-tested (CF runs Hydra), full OAuth/OIDC; cost: new substrate dep, new SQL backend, duplicates trust-root concerns.

B. **Implement the spec slice in-stack** (~2-3k LOC TypeScript inside the existing notme Worker) — reuses notme's Ed25519 master for JWT issuance; trust root stays inside Interlace pipeline; ART takes responsibility for spec compliance. **Recommended.**

## Scope shape

`worker/src/oauth/` — authorize.ts, consent.ts, token.ts (extend existing), introspect.ts, revoke.ts, apps-registry.ts, auth-code-state.ts, pkce.ts. Cloister-side: extend `cloister.capnp` `identity-bridge` route paths under the same `wellKnownIdentityBridge` route kind (no new tenant; same trust boundary).

## Open decisions before implementation

1. Consent UI hosting: same Worker, or R2-hosted page + state callback? (Recommend: same Worker.)
2. Apps registry storage: new DO class, or extend notme's DO? (Recommend: extend existing.)
3. Token-lifetime defaults: align with CF's "multiple hours" or with Interlace's short-lease posture? (Recommend: short-lease Interlace-aligned.)
4. OAuth scopes: 1:1 mirror of Interlace scope vocabulary, or curated subset? (Recommend: 1:1 initially; add curation when external devs ask.)

## Why P2

Product-direction question, not substrate gap. ART works today with Interlace-only authn. The OAuth surface unlocks external developer adoption — ecosystem play, not a reliability fix. Land after substrate-trust layer is stable but before first external developer onboarding push.

## Full design

Staged at `docs/design/011-external-oauth-provider.md` (commit pending) — covers context, decision matrix, scope shape, file tree, all four open questions, and out-of-scope (SSO/SAML federation; centralized hosting; refresh-token leaked-token detection).

## Out of scope

- Replacing Interlace cert-based authn for internal substrate trust. Interlace stays the substrate-tier mechanism.
- SSO / SAML / corporate-IdP federation.
- Centralized hosting (à la Auth0 / Clerk). notme stays self-hosted by the cluster operator.

## Related

- https://blog.cloudflare.com/oauth-for-all/
- cloister.capnp identity-bridge tenant + ADR-0007 (Interlace), ADR-0018 (notme co-location)
- `~/remotes/art/notme/docs/design/011-external-oauth-provider.md` (staged)

Drift to reconcile when revived: doc 011 lists /oauth/authorize as ✗ missing, but worker/src/signing-authority.ts:342-359 already has mintRedirectToken "used by the /authorize redirect flow," and worker/src/auth/ has passkey + principals + federated-OIDC + connections. The design doc undercounts what's already built. The JWT-minting primitive it would consume is notme-d87ef2 (dispatched standalone).

title: P1: /authorize redirect mints DPoP-bound token — rejected by cnf check
description: /authorize page calls POST /token which mints a DPoP-bound token (cnf.jkt). After the cnf downgrade fix, verifyAccessToken correctly rejects tokens with cnf. The redirect flow is broken.\n\nFix: mint an unbound redirect token inside the DO (no cnf claim). Short-lived, single-use, EdDSA-signed. The /authorize page calls this instead of /token.

title: Expose JSON CABundle endpoint at /internal/ca-bundle for cloister consumption
description:
Surfaced 2026-05-09 from the cloister-side fetcher work (cloister-b89fdb).

## Background

cloister's lease middleware (cloister-bd7770) consumes a signed JSON `CABundle` to verify Signet ephemeral certs. The bundle shape is what notme already uses internally (`notme/worker/src/revocation.ts:CABundle`):

```
interface CABundle {
  epoch: number;
  seqno: number;
  keys: Record<string, string>;        // kid → b64-std raw Ed25519 pubkey
  keyId: string;
  prevKeyId?: string;
  issuedAt: number;                    // Unix-seconds
  signature: string;                   // Ed25519 over bundleCanonical, b64-std
}
```

Today notme exposes `/.well-known/ca-bundle.pem` (PEM-formatted X.509). cloister needs the raw JSON bundle (not PEM) because:
- The Interlace cert chain is Ed25519 raw-key, not X.509 hierarchies
- cloister's `bundleCanonical` (lifted from notme/revocation.ts) produces the canonical bytes that signet's Go side signs

## What to do

Add a service-binding-only endpoint at `/internal/ca-bundle` that:
1. Returns `Content-Type: application/json` with the current `CABundle` JSON
2. Calls `SIGNING_AUTHORITY.getCurrentCABundle()` (or whatever the existing internal accessor is named) to fetch the latest signed bundle
3. Sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=240` (4 min — must stay strictly inside notme's `BUNDLE_MAX_AGE_MS = 5min` so cloister's 4-min refresh interval always sees a non-stale bundle; per cloister-e195ea audit amendment)
4. Returns 503 if no bundle is currently signed (cloister fails closed, then retries)

The endpoint MUST NOT be reachable from external HTTP (no Authorization-by-default-routes; restrict to service-binding callers via the existing internal-only path policy).

## Contract with cloister

cloister's fetcher: `cloister/src/storage/notme-bundle-fetcher.ts:notmeBundleFetcher`
- Calls `env.NOTME.fetch(new Request("https://notme-bot/internal/ca-bundle", { method: "GET" }))`
- Expects `200` + JSON body matching the CABundle shape
- Treats anything else as `null` (fail-closed via cloister's getCABundle)

cloister verifies the bundle's Ed25519 signature against `INTERLACE_ROOT_PUBKEY` after fetching, so this endpoint doesn't need to gate on the caller's identity — the signature is the trust anchor. But adding the service-binding restriction is defense-in-depth.

## Acceptance

- `/internal/ca-bundle` returns the current signed bundle as JSON
- The endpoint is unreachable from public HTTP (service-binding-only)
- A test in notme demonstrates signing the bundle once + serving it via the endpoint
- Cross-repo smoke: cloister's `task smoke` (when it runs against a notme replica) successfully fetches + verifies the bundle

## Files (notme-side)

- `notme/worker/worker.ts` — add the `/internal/ca-bundle` route
- `notme/worker/src/revocation.ts` — likely already has the bundle accessor; expose if needed
- `notme/worker/src/__tests__/internal-ca-bundle.test.ts` (NEW) — round-trip via the service binding

## Refs

- cloister-bd7770 — lease middleware (consumer)
- cloister-c614ae — bundle signature verification
- cloister-e195ea — CA bundle cache + 4-min refresh interval
- ADR-0007 audit amendment 2026-05-08 (cloister)

title: THREAT_MODEL claims the /authorize redirect token is DPoP-bound; it is an unbound bearer in a URL
description:
Found during adversarial review of PR #55 (notme-e1700d), 2026-08-03. NOT introduced by that PR — pre-existing on main.

THREAT_MODEL.md §5 (DPoP authorize redirect), row `token in URL logs`, states the mitigation as:

  "token is DPoP-bound (useless without ephemeral key), 5-min expiry, JTI unique"

The DPoP-bound half is FALSE, and it is the half doing the security work in that sentence.

Evidence chain, all verified at HEAD:

1. worker.ts:1814-1815 — the route's own comment: "POST /authorize/token — Unbound redirect token for /authorize flow. Session cookie required. No DPoP — token has no cnf.jkt."
2. worker.ts:1860 — the route calls `authority.mintRedirectToken(...)`, not the DPoP mint.
3. signing-authority.ts:433 — inside `mintRedirectToken`: "// No jkt — unbound token, accepted by verifyAccessToken". `mintAccessToken` only attaches `cnf` when `jkt` is truthy (auth/token.ts), so the minted JWT has no confirmation claim at all.
4. worker.ts:1866-1870 — responds `token_type: "Bearer"`.
5. worker.ts:926/933/937 — the `/authorize` page script then puts it in a URL and navigates:
     var token = data.access_token;
     var dest = redirectUri + sep + 'token=' + encodeURIComponent(token);
     window.location.href = dest;

So a plain bearer credential is written into a URL query parameter. Anyone who can read it from browser history, a Referer header, an intermediary proxy log, or the receiving server's own access log holds a working credential until it expires. "Useless without the ephemeral key" is exactly wrong: there is no key.

This is the defect class the project exists to eliminate — a bearer asset documented as proof-of-possession. The docs being wrong is worse than the code being weak, because the threat model is what a reviewer checks INSTEAD of re-deriving the property.

Mitigations that DO survive and should be what the row claims: 5-minute expiry, unique jti, audience allowlist (`getAllowedAudiences`, worker.ts:1843), and redirect_uri validation (`validateRedirectUri`, worker.ts:1776).

The comment at signing-authority.ts:422 gives the design reason the token is unbound — the /authorize flow's DPoP keypair is ephemeral and lost across the navigation — so this is a real constraint, not an oversight in the code. The bug is the threat model asserting a mitigation that was designed away.

Two things to do, in order:
1. CORRECT the THREAT_MODEL row to state the actual mitigations and name the residual exposure explicitly (bearer-in-URL, bounded by 5 min). Cheap, and it stops the false claim propagating.
2. THEN decide whether the residual is acceptable. Options if not: deliver via fragment (`#token=`) instead of query so it is not sent to the server or logged; POST the token to the redirect target instead of navigating; or a one-time exchange code redeemed by the receiving app (RFC 6749 §4.1 shape) so the URL carries a single-use code rather than the credential.

Related: docs/design/012-sender-constrained-oidc.md makes exactly this argument about id_tokens being bearer assertions. The same reasoning applies here and was not carried across.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to the fix in PR #56, caught before merge.

The first pass added `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` to the /authorize page and described it as stopping the browser from handing the token-bearing URL to third parties. **That was wrong and overstated the fix.**

A Referrer-Policy on a document governs the Referer THAT document sends — its own subresource loads, and the navigation away to redirect_uri. It does not govern what the DESTINATION page sends once the browser is sitting on `${redirect_uri}?token=...`. That is the destination's own Referrer-Policy (rig's), and it is the vector that actually forwards the access token onward. notme cannot close it from the /authorize page.

What the header does protect: the authorize URL itself, which carries `state` (a CSRF value), from being sent onward. Modest — modern browsers default to `strict-origin-when-cross-origin` and would send only the origin anyway, so this mostly makes an existing default explicit and covers the same-origin case. Keeping it (correct hygiene), but it is NOT a mitigation for this row and the comment, threat-model row and test now say so.

BLAST RADIUS, now established concretely. One consumer: `rig/web/src/index.ts:396` redirects to `auth.notme.bot/authorize` for the `/admin/setup-github` flow, and line 355 reads the token back with `c.req.query('token')` — a SERVER-SIDE query read. Consequences:

- The token reaches rig's Cloudflare Worker in the request line, so it lands in Cloudflare's access logs. This is the largest unmitigated vector, larger than the Referer one.
- A fragment-based fix (`#token=`) would BREAK rig outright — fragments never reach the server. rig would need client-side JS to read `location.hash` and hand it over out-of-band.

Corrected residual, all unmitigated:
1. Token in browser history on the user's machine.
2. Token in the destination's server/access logs (verified above).
3. Onward Referer leakage from the destination page — governed by rig, not notme.

Bounding facts that keep this moderate rather than critical: 5-minute lifetime; `aud` pins it to ONE resource server so it is not a general-purpose credential; unique jti; it is an access token, not a session, so it cannot be used to mint more; and the flow is a rarely-exercised admin path.

Options to actually remove it, ranked:
1. **Single-use exchange code** (RFC 6749 §4.1). The URL carries a code, not a credential; a logged code is worthless once redeemed. Correct long-term shape and where ADR-011 already points (it lists `/oauth/authorize` + code exchange as missing). Needs a rig change.
2. **Fragment** (`#token=`). Removes vectors 2 and 3 outright — fragments are never sent to servers and never appear in a Referer. Cheapest real improvement. Needs a rig change (server-side read becomes client-side).
3. **POST-to-target** (auto-submitting form). Token in a body, not a URL. Needs a rig change.

All three are coordinated cross-repo changes. Not doing any of them unilaterally — filing the decision here. Recommend (1) since ADR-011 is already headed there, with (2) as a stopgap if the admin flow needs hardening sooner.

title: bug(dpop): enforce proof alg/key pairing and reject private JWK material
description: RFC 9449 section 4.3 requires an acceptable asymmetric alg and requires the embedded proof JWK to contain no private key. The shared verifier currently ignores pHeader.alg, selects verification from kty/crv, and does not reject `d`/other private members. Pin ES256 to EC P-256 and EdDSA to OKP Ed25519, reject mismatches/unsupported algorithms with stable codes, and reject private JWK material before import. Mirror the private-key rejection in worker token-endpoint validation.

comments.text: Implemented test-first: proof alg is now pinned to ES256/EC P-256 or EdDSA/OKP Ed25519, private JWK members are rejected before import, malformed imports and verify failures map to stable DPoPVerificationError codes, and worker token-endpoint validation rejects private JWK material. Fresh `task worker:check` passes (371 tests + 6 todo; 18 worker-pool tests), package build/format pass. Awaiting final reviewer verdict and commit.

title: Audit + ship OCI image `notme:0.1.0` consumable by cloister cluster.capnp
description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from cloister's deployment-readiness audit.

## What needs to happen

cloister's `cluster.capnp` (the multi-bundle deployment manifest at `~/remotes/art/cloister/cluster.capnp`) expects an OCI image tagged **`notme:0.1.0`** for the `notme-identity` bundle. cloister's `task cluster:up` invokes a compose runtime (nerdctl/podman/docker) and assumes this image is locally available (or pullable from a registry).

Today notme has apko + melange configs at:
- `packages/apko-notme.yaml`
- `packages/melange-workerd.yaml`
- `packages/melange-notme-app.yaml`

But it's not clear from outside notme whether `task image` (or equivalent) actually:
1. Produces an image tagged `notme:0.1.0`.
2. Bundles the worker (`worker/dist/`) into the image at a path workerd can boot from.
3. Embeds `worker/wrangler.toml`-equivalent config that lets it serve on port 8788 (the port cluster.capnp expects).
4. Survives `docker load < notme.tar` + `docker run -p 8788:8788 notme:0.1.0` → 200 on `/health`.

## Acceptance

- `task image` (or whatever the build target is — name it if different) produces `notme.tar` or pushes to a local registry.
- `docker load < notme.tar` (or pull) makes `notme:0.1.0` available locally.
- `docker run -p 8788:8788 notme:0.1.0` boots and responds 200 on `/health` (or notme's equivalent liveness endpoint).
- Document the build invocation in notme's README so a cloister operator can reproduce it.
- If the apko configs need updates (version pin, port, entrypoint), update them.
- If notme has its OWN cluster.capnp / equivalent topology, mention how the two compose (cross-link).

## Cross-repo context

- **cloister** at `~/remotes/art/cloister/cluster.capnp` declares `image = "notme:0.1.0"` for the `notme-identity` bundle.
- The wire from cloister-router to notme is the workerd service binding (named `NOTME` in cloister-router's bindings, pointing at notme-identity via `serviceBindingProxy` for `/identity/*`).
- For the simple-deploy "docker run cloister-bundled" story, see cloister-side bead `cloister-db99cd` (whether to co-locate notme inside cloister's workerd as a single image — different question; this bead is the separate-container path).

## Refs

- cloister's `~/remotes/art/cloister/cluster.capnp` (the consuming manifest)
- cloister's `~/remotes/art/cloister/docs/deployment/cluster-in-a-pod.md` (operator guide that calls into this)
- cloister-db99cd (sibling: should notme co-locate instead of ship separately?)

## Out of scope

- Co-location with cloister (that's `cloister-db99cd`).
- Multi-tenant scaling of notme (separate concern).
- Anything beyond producing a runnable, tagged image.

the entrypoint serves 8788, and `release.yml` now pushes to

Not closing — two items here are genuinely still open and were out of scope

title: notme as identity for entire.io: federation machinery exists, gated on their trusted-issuer list + our ADR-011
description:
What it would take to use notme as identity for entire.io (Git + agent-session checkpointing; entireio/cli is Go/MIT/4.9k stars — core and auth server are closed source).

## What Entire runs today (verified against their code and live endpoints)

- Standard OIDC AS at https://us.auth.entire.io (regional: us/eu/au/in). Discovery advertises authorization_code, device_code, RFC 8693 token-exchange, RFC 7523 jwt-bearer, PKCE S256, and id_token_signing_alg_values_supported [EdDSA, RS256].
- tls_client_certificate_bound_access_tokens: true (RFC 8705) but NO mtls_endpoint_aliases and NO DPoP.
- CLI flow: browser/device login -> login JWT -> RFC 8693 exchange at the core /oauth/token for repo-scoped tokens (internal/entireclient/httputil/oauth.go, TokenExchangeForm). subject_token_type is hardcoded to access_token.
- ENTIRE_TOKEN env var is the documented CI/workload-identity bypass: "a runner injects a short-lived login or sa-session JWT".
- Core API has /service-accounts/{id}/bindings where a Binding is {providerId, attributeFilter} — the standard OIDC-federation primitive, same shape as GCP WIF and octo-sts trust policies.
- `entire login --server <url>` is a first-class flag; ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL was retired in favour of it.

## Blocker on their side

https://entire.io/.well-known/entire-api.json publishes a FIXED trusted_issuers list: the four *.auth.entire.io regional servers, nothing else. /api/v1/oidc-providers is GET-only (no POST) and returns 401. No self-service way to register an external issuer, and the CLI has no command touching it, so it is console/admin-side.

The federation machinery Entire would need in order to accept notme already exists and is already wired. The only missing piece is an entry in a server-side list we cannot write. That makes this a small, well-shaped ask of them rather than an architecture change.

## Blocker on our side

ADR-013 deliberately keeps authorization_endpoint and code_challenge_methods_supported in FORBIDDEN_METADATA_FIELDS because publishing them advertises "notme is an OAuth AS you can integrate with" — and there is still no client registry and no consent screen behind it. That is ADR-011 (Proposed, unimplemented). Third-party federation with Entire is precisely the case ADR-013 was withholding those fields to prevent, so ADR-011 is a hard prerequisite for the clean path.

## Compatibility that already lines up

- notme signs EdDSA/Ed25519; Entire accepts EdDSA id_tokens.
- notme serves /.well-known/openid-configuration and /.well-known/jwks.json live — exactly what their jwks_uris map consumes.
- Issuer https://auth.notme.bot is stable and HTTPS.
- notme already mints from GHA OIDC, which is the identity their CI path wants.

## Options, cheapest first

1. Custodian, not issuer (needs no cooperation). notme fronts the Entire credential: GHA OIDC -> notme cert -> notme vends a short-lived Entire login JWT it holds. Entire sees a normal Entire token. HONEST CAVEAT: this moves the secret into notme rather than eliminating it — you still bootstrap from an Entire-issued refresh/sa token. Weaker than it looks. Ties to notme-724300 (secretless proxy).
2. Ask them to add https://auth.notme.bot as an OIDC provider, then bind a service account with an attributeFilter. Requires ADR-011 first. This is the real integration and uses only machinery they already ship.
3. Differentiated angle. Their CI tokens are bearer tokens; they advertise mTLS binding but ship no mtls_endpoint_aliases and no DPoP. notme does cert identity + RFC 9449 DPoP. This is where notme is additive rather than duplicative, and the strongest thing to lead with when talking to them.

## Footgun worth raising with them

CreateBindingInputBody.attributeFilter is documented as "Exact-match key/value map; empty filter matches any token." An empty filter means any identity from that issuer can assume the service account — the misconfiguration class behind real GCP Workload Identity Federation breaches. Fail-closed (require a non-empty filter) would be the safer default.

## Already banked

Fixed while doing this assessment: FORBIDDEN_METADATA_FIELDS comments claimed "PKCE is unimplemented" (ADR-013 shipped S256) and had never been narrowed the way ADR-013 said they would be. Branch notme-as-metadata-pkce-comment.
acceptance_criteria: Decision recorded on which of the three integration options to pursue, and (if option 2) a concrete ask sent to Entire. Superseded if Entire ships self-service OIDC provider registration.

title: Replace keyIdFromSpki with the canonical BLAKE3 kid; epoch-rotate JWKS; keep opaque-match
description:
notme currently derives its JWK `kid` via `keyIdFromSpki` (RFC-7638-ish truncated SHA-256 over SPKI DER — worker/src/key-id.ts, per worker/README.md:182). Switch to the canonical derivation defined by signet (BLAKE3 over the raw Ed25519 public key, 128-bit) so an LLO signed head's signerKid and a cloister verifier resolve against notme's JWKS.

Scope:
1. Replace keyIdFromSpki with the canonical kid. Publish it in both `/.well-known/jwks.json` (keys[].kid) AND the JWT header kid — they must move together.
2. Because kid is opaque-matched by consumers (worker.js:37085 `keys.find(k => k.kid === header.kid)`), the change is safe as a key-rotation/epoch event: bump the epoch so caches (1hr TTL) refresh. No external consumer recomputes the kid (Cloudflare Access is upstream of notme, not a downstream kid consumer — verified 2026-07-21).
3. Add a test gating notme's kid against signet's pinned vector fixture.

Note: `keyIdFromSpki` may still be needed anywhere an X.509 SubjectKeyId is expected — do not delete it blindly; scope its remaining callers first. This bead is about the PROTOCOL kid (JWKS/JWT), not the cert SubjectKeyId.

Close condition: `cd ~/remotes/art/notme && <the JS test runner, e.g. pnpm -C worker test>` green including the new vector-conformance test.

The 'epoch-rotate JWKS' half: new keys get 128-bit kids via the existing rotation mechanism (no new code); retiring 64-bit prevKeyId comparators is R3 (signet-3723b6). Also implements the notme half of signet-371778 (R2).

title: Verify against CF production whether Ed25519 SPKI import accepts a P-256 key
description:
Found 2026-08-04 while building /cert/passkey. Fixed forward in that PR; this bead is only about establishing the production blast radius, which I could not do from here.

THE BUG (fixed): `importPublicKey` (worker/src/cert-authority.ts) did "try Ed25519, fall back to ECDSA P-256 on throw". On workerd the Ed25519 import ACCEPTS a P-256 SPKI rather than throwing, so the fallback never ran and every key returned as `{name:"Ed25519"}`.

Reproduced in the vitest-pool-workers suite (real workerd):

    imported alg: {"name":"Ed25519"}     // from a P-256 SPKI
    spki roundtrip identical: true
    verify w/ ORIGINAL key: true
    verify w/ importPublicKey key: THREW —
      Requested algorithm "ECDSA" does not match this CryptoKey's algorithm "Ed25519"

CONSEQUENCE: the P-256 proof-of-possession check on every cert-issuing path — /cert/gha, /cert, /cert/passkey — threw and was caught as a 401. The certificate itself would have been fine (SPKI bytes round-trip intact); the failure is at PoP verification, and the 401 reads as "your proof is bad" when the proof is correct.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR: I verified this against workerd as run by vitest-pool-workers. I did NOT verify Cloudflare's production build. Those can differ, and the difference decides whether this was a live production outage on /cert/gha (the primary CI identity path) or only ever affected local and CI.

Two readings, and they have very different implications:
- If prod behaves the same, /cert/gha has been rejecting valid GHA PoP proofs with 401 for as long as the try/catch has been there. That seems like something someone would have noticed, which is mild evidence AGAINST this reading.
- If prod's Ed25519 import correctly rejects a P-256 SPKI, the fallback worked there and the bug was confined to workerd-local and the CI suite.

HOW TO CHECK: exercise /cert/gha against the deployed worker with a real GHA OIDC token and real P-256 + Ed25519 ephemeral keys, and confirm a 200 rather than a 401 "P-256 proof-of-possession failed". The action already does exactly this — a green run of the GHA identity workflow against production, on a commit BEFORE the fix, answers it. `gh run list --workflow=gha-identity.yml` history may already contain the answer without running anything.

WHY IT WENT UNNOTICED, worth recording separately: `grep -rn importPublicKey src/__tests__` was EMPTY. Three call sites depended on it (cert-exchange.ts, cert-authority.ts, auth/derive-credentials.ts), each with its own coverage; the shared primitive underneath had none. Tests clustered at the level people reason about. src/import-public-key.do.test.ts now covers it.

Note derive-credentials.ts was unaffected in practice: it imports the CA public key, which IS Ed25519, so the wrong-algorithm import happened to be the right one.
acceptance_criteria: Established, with evidence, whether CF production's Ed25519 SPKI import accepts a P-256 key — e.g. a pre-fix production /cert/gha run that returned 200, or a deliberate probe. Result recorded on this bead and, if prod was affected, the incident window stated.

title: POC: load tree-root hash → instantiate notme-proxy + tiny HTTP echo Worker as a unit (math-friend's smallest viable end-to-end)
description:
Math-friend's recommended smallest-viable POC for the operadic-Merkle-DAG substrate (`ley-line-3278b4`). End-to-end before any schema decisions land. If it works, the rest is fleshing out the picture; if it doesn't, the whole frame needs rethinking.

## What to build

- Existing notme-proxy (Rust, holds in-memory mTLS key — never extracted, never shared).
- 50-line HTTP echo Worker (workerd-runnable; trivial).
- Hash both as chunks per the substrate ADR's chunk schema.
- 200-line Rust loader that takes a single tree-root hash and instantiates them as a unit.
- Verify: HTTP request through the loader → echo Worker sees mTLS-attached request from notme-proxy.

## Why it matters

This is the empirical falsifier for the entire substrate frame. Either the loader-from-tree-root model produces a working composed deployment OR it doesn't. No amount of ADR refinement substitutes for this measurement.

## DO NOT START until

- `ley-line-3278b4` (substrate ADR) has answers — chunk schema, capability resolution, identity model picked.
- `notme-32c72f` (cloister re-survey) is done — POC may need to consume cloister output, depending on what re-survey reveals.

If you start before those answers, you'll bake in arbitrary choices the substrate ADR is supposed to derive.

## Hard constraint (architectural decision 2026-04-29)

notme-proxy stays where it is, NOT extracted to a generic `cloister-companion`. The mTLS key lives in notme-proxy memory and never appears in any chunk content. The chunk is a *manifest* describing how a deployment binds notme-proxy as a capability; the key crosses no chunk boundary.

## Acceptance

- HTTP echo Worker receives a request bearing the mTLS identity from notme-proxy.
- The composed unit is loadable from a single tree-root hash.
- Loader is ≤300 LOC of Rust (math-friend's 200-LOC target + 50% slack).
- Spike branch only — DO NOT merge the loader into a notme/ley-line crate without ADR sign-off.

## Anchors

- `ley-line-3278b4` (substrate ADR — blocks this)
- `notme-32c72f` (cloister re-survey — blocks this)
- `notme-e005a8` (mTLS-injector chunk spec — companion)

title: Emit artifact-only server.json via leyline-mcp-descriptor v0.13.0
description:
LLO v0.13.0 shipped everything this was waiting on; the emit side is unblocked TODAY (full brief: ley-line-open/_agent_log/2026-07-30-for-notme.md).

- Binary: leyline-mcp-descriptor-{linux,darwin}-{amd64,arm64} in the v0.13.0 release assets, SHA256SUMS-verified.
- Shape: packages[] OMITTED entirely (never a placeholder transport); _meta.'io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided'.artifacts = [{registryType:'oci', identifier:'ghcr.io/agentic-research/notme' (TAGLESS), version:'<tag>'}, {…notme-proxy…}]. Artifact entries pass the same tagless-identifier + version validation as packages entries.
- The rendered notme-shaped example is already the contract fixture on cloister-02dd65 — emit exactly that.
- Wire regeneration into notme's release flow with a stale-check (LLO's gen:server-json:check pattern) so a version bump can't leave the descriptor behind.
- Caveat, stated so it isn't discovered the hard way: cloister's CONSUMER (cloister-02dd65) is still open — end-to-end OCI-pin derivation validates when they land. Emitting now is safe; the shape cannot drift without breaking LLO's own generated conformance.

comments.text:
DONE. server.json is now artifact-only and, for the first time, actually
validated against the schema it declares.

## Verified before writing anything

- v0.13.0 release exists; `leyline-mcp-descriptor-darwin-arm64` downloaded and
  checksum-matched against the release `SHA256SUMS`
  (`b5e9c49fbbcc7a08…6fe609`).
- The shape is legal, from the schema rather than from the brief:
  `ServerDetail.required` is `["name","description","version"]` — `packages` is
  NOT required — and
  `_meta."io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"` is declared
  `additionalProperties: true`, so `artifacts` is a sanctioned occupant.
- `Package.required` really is `["registryType","identifier","transport"]`,
  confirming notme-6e5330's finding at the source.

## The artifacts block matches the emitter, proven not assumed

Fed a notme descriptor to the v0.13.0 binary and diffed its rendered
publisher-provided block against the committed file:

    diff <(jq -S '._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"]' llo-rendered.json) \
         <(jq -S '._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"]' server.json)
    -> IDENTICAL

## Hand-maintained, not generated — with a measured reason

Running the emitter showed exactly what a generated file would cost. Its
output has no `title`, no `websiteUrl`, and `_meta` is a closed two-field
struct (`art.cloister/v1` for tool-group claims, `publisher-provided`).
Adopting it wholesale would drop five things:

  1. `title`
  2. `websiteUrl`
  3. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/surface"`
  4. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/packages"`
  5. `_meta."art.cloister/v1".bundles[]` — the notme-identity / notme-proxy
     hypervisor-tier topology (ADR-0011/0018/0005), ~40 lines that are notme's
     own and not derivable from an image address

(5) is the sharp one: the crate puts TOOL-GROUP claims under that same
`art.cloister/v1` key, and omits the key entirely when there are no groups.
notme has no groups, so a generated file silently drops the block rather than
colliding with it. The input shape is also documented upstream as "This input
shape WILL change."

So: the file stays hand-maintained and matches the emitter where the contract
lives (the artifacts array). This is answer (b) on notme-450c3c's acceptance
criteria — adoption rejected on measured evidence, with the reason recorded in
the file's own `_meta`.

## The drift check the bead asked for, in two halves

`task server:check` (new, wired into ci.yml's `check` job) and
`task version:check VERSION=<tag>` (existing, runs before every publish).
Neither subsumes the other: nothing on a branch knows the release tag, so the
PR gate can't assert it — and running ONLY the release gate is precisely how
both known defects reached main. `--self` says so in its own success output
instead of implying it checked a tag it never saw.

New assertions, each falsification-tested by mutating the file and confirming
a non-zero exit:

  - schema conformance via ajv against a VENDORED, sha256-pinned copy of the
    2025-12-11 schema (`schema/mcp/server.schema.2025-12-11.json`, byte-identical
    to both the canonical URL and LLO's copy — 3fba0959…14de0)
  - `packages` key refused outright (regression gate — the old shape can only
    come back as a schema violation or a fabricated transport)
  - top-level `version` must agree too
  - artifacts entries keep BOTH halves of ADR-0041 §2: absent version fatal,
    tagged identifier fatal, checked per-entry with exact tag-stripped matching

## It found a second, unknown defect on its first run

`/description: must NOT have more than 100 characters` — the description was
135. Unrelated to the transport bug, never checked by anything, and it would
have been rejected by any registry validating on ingest. Shortened to 87.

That is the argument for the PR gate in one line: notme-6e5330 was found by
another repo, and this one was found by the check, not by us.

## Not yet end-to-end

cloister-02dd65 (the consumer that derives OCI pins from this extension) is
still open — verified, not taken from the brief. Emitting now is safe and the
shape cannot drift without breaking LLO's own generated conformance, but the
full derive path lights up only when that lands.

Files: server.json, scripts/check-image-versions.ts,
schema/mcp/server.schema.2025-12-11.json, Taskfile.yml,
.github/workflows/ci.yml, .gitignore, packages/README.md, scripts/README.md
(the bead's `files` said only package.json, which was wrong — noting it so a
future dispatch scopes correctly).
comments.author: rsry-mcp

acceptance_criteria: notme + notme-proxy descriptors emitted with no packages[] and _meta artifacts entries matching the cloister-02dd65 fixture; regeneration wired into release with a drift check

title: notme: GitHub Actions disabled at repo level — 7 open PRs have no CI signal
description:
Discovered while checking why PR #2-#8 (opened in this session) have no CI status. The workflow file at `.github/workflows/ci.yml` looks fine and lists as "active" via `gh workflow list`, but `gh api repos/agentic-research/notme/actions/permissions` returns:

```json
{"enabled":false,"sha_pinning_required":false}
```

That's an org/repo-level kill switch. Workflows can't fire while it's set. Confirms why:
- "Test Identity Exchange" workflow only ran via `workflow_dispatch` (manual trigger that sometimes ignores the disable, depending on org policy)
- CI workflow has `total_count: 0` historical runs since 7aa843d added it 4 weeks ago
- All 7 of this session's PRs (PR #2 through #8) have empty `statusCheckRollup`

**Fix:** enable Actions on the repo. UI path: Settings → Actions → General → "Allow all actions and reusable workflows" (or your preferred policy). API path:
```
gh api -X PUT repos/agentic-research/notme/actions/permissions \
  --input - <<<'{"enabled":true,"allowed_actions":"all"}'
```

Once enabled, push/PR triggers fire and CI signal returns. The 7 open PRs would re-run by closing+reopening or pushing an empty commit.

**Why it was disabled is the operator question** — possibly turned off during the security audit work (rosary-b22de6 hardening pass) or org-level cost control. Re-enabling needs explicit operator decision.

This is the operator action; an agent shouldn't flip the kill switch.

Side note: even with this disabled, I've been verifying tsc + vitest locally on every commit — but external CI would catch environmental drift (Node version, lockfile mismatch, etc.) that local doesn't.

title: Conform notme-proxy's MCP surface to the sessionless 2026-07-28 protocol pin
description:
LLO pinned the MCP wire schema: vendored protocol.2026-07-28.json, digest ef70b61f99b6d2e5e3b46863822eab08dff6a45bedc7a08914e0e5b133f40203, gated at COMPILE time on the LLO side. The pinned protocol is sessionless — no initialize (SEP-2567/2575 removed sessions) and no ping. If notme-proxy speaks MCP (either direction):

1. Remove/refuse initialize and ping rather than tolerating them — LLO's daemon refuses them with a do-not-extend posture (LLO bead 1227f2 tracks the daemon handshake hardening).
2. Add a conformance test that fetches or vendors the SAME protocol.2026-07-28.json and asserts its digest, so drift on either side fails a test rather than an integration.
3. Method names should come from the schema (LLO generates METHOD_* consts from $defs[].properties.method.const — same technique works in TS).

Reference: ley-line-open/rs/ll-core/mcp-protocol-schema/ and ley-line-open/_agent_log/2026-07-30-for-notme.md.

comments.text:
NO-OP — notme-proxy has no MCP surface to conform. Verified 2026-07-30, not assumed.

The bead is correctly conditional ("If notme-proxy speaks MCP (either
direction)"). It does not, in either direction:

    $ grep -rniE 'jsonrpc|\bmcp\b|initialize|tools/list' proxy/
    proxy/README.md:20:        agent["agent / CLI / MCP"]

One hit, in a mermaid node label naming the *client* upstream of the proxy.
`proxy/src/main.rs` is 1031 lines and its whole surface is transport:
`parse_listen_addr`, `load_certs_and_key`, `build_mtls_config`,
`validate_uds_path`, `proxy_to_uds`, `handle_uds`, `dispatch`, `handle_proxy`.
No JSON-RPC dependency in `proxy/Cargo.toml` — no serde_json, no jsonrpc crate.
The UDS path, per the module docstring, "writes the request body verbatim,
half-closes, reads bytes-back, returns them in a 200."

So the proxy CARRIES MCP bytes and never parses them. There is no `initialize`
to remove because there is nothing that could send or recognise one, and no
method-name table to generate from `$defs[].properties.method.const` because
no method names appear in the code.

## The pin is worth knowing anyway — it confirms the design

The 2026-07-28 schema being SESSIONLESS (SEP-2567/2575 removed sessions) is
load-bearing news for this proxy in the opposite direction from the bead's
framing. The UDS mode is strictly one-shot: write body → half-close → read
bytes → 200. A sessionful protocol requiring a persistent stream across an
`initialize` handshake could NOT be carried over that shape. Sessionless can.

The pin therefore validates the existing transport rather than requiring a
change to it. Worth recording because the reverse — MCP re-growing sessions —
WOULD be a real break here, and it would break at the transport layer where
nothing currently looks for it.

## Recommend

Close as no-op. Item 2 (a conformance test pinning LLO's schema digest) is not
worth adding: a digest assertion over a schema nothing in this repo reads
tests only that a file was downloaded. Refile if notme ever grows an MCP
surface — at which point `_meta` in server.json must move from `artifacts`
back to `packages[]` WITH a real transport, and that is the moment the pin
starts to bite.

Cross-ref: notme-38044e (artifact-only server.json, landed) records the same
"notme serves no MCP" fact in the file cloister actually reads.

title: schema-bridge: handle Go-annotation declarations so task gen:zod runs on notme/schema/identity.capnp
description:
**Re-filed from rosary-8d2c78** (reconciler-busted; re-filed in target repo).

Surfaced during B.3 (schema-bridge lift in PR #21 — merged).

# Issue
`task gen:zod` against `notme/schema/identity.capnp` errors with `unmapped capnp construct annotation at node id=bea97f1023792be0`. Root cause: `identity.capnp` uses `$Go.package`/`$Go.import` for the existing `schema:go` task; capnp emits the imported `/go.capnp`'s annotation **declarations** as `Node.Annotation` nodes, which schema-bridge rejects at `packages/schema-bridge/src/inputs/capnp.rs:128-130`. Zero impact on zod output (the annotations describe Go codegen) but trips schema-bridge's fail-fast policy.

# Three fix options (recommend option 2)

**Option 1**: Allow ALL annotation declarations to be skipped (loosens the fail-fast policy across the board — fragile).

**Option 2 (RECOMMENDED)**: Allowlist the Go annotation file id `@0xd12a1c51fedd6c88` alongside the existing `ANN_JSON_*` constants in `packages/schema-bridge/src/inputs/capnp.rs`. Surgical, preserves fail-fast for everything else.

**Option 3**: Strip Go annotations from notme/schema/identity.capnp at codegen time (preprocessor). Doesn't scale to other annotation systems.

# Done when
- `task gen:zod` succeeds against notme/schema/identity.capnp
- Committed baseline `notme/gen/ts/identity.zod.ts`
- `task gen:zod:check-drift` works as designed

# Depends on
- nothing (PR #21 already landed schema-bridge in notme/packages/)

title: ADR hygiene: extend @doc-check to ADRs 005-012, resolve duplicate numbers, backfill Status lines
description:
Full ADR-vs-code audit run 2026-08-04. Findings, and what is left after the mechanical fixes already applied.

## The systemic issue

`task docs:check` reports "All 35 claims verified" and is green. It covers 5 of 14 design docs — only those carrying the @doc-check annotation: 006, 013, 014, 015, 016. ADRs 005, 007 (x2), 008, 009, 010, 011, 012 (x2) are entirely unverified prose.

That is not a coincidence in where drift was found: every stale claim in this audit was in an uncovered doc. The gate reads as comprehensive while covering the recent minority, and nothing in its output says otherwise. It should report coverage (docs checked / docs total), and every design doc should either carry @doc-check or an explicit opt-out with a reason.

## Fixed in this pass (branch notme-as-metadata-pkce-comment)

- ADR-011 gap table listed /oauth/authorize, PKCE, and code->token exchange as missing. ADR-013 shipped all three. Third instance of this rot in the same file family.
- ADR-011 Bead line said "(TBD - bd embeddeddolt format mismatch)". notme-0078a9 was filed 2026-06-25 and scopes docs/design/011-external-oauth-provider.md.
- 007-secretless-local-proxy, 007-secretless-plan, 008, 009 had NO Status line. Backfilled with audited status.
- as-metadata.ts: two comments and one published value justified by claims ADR-013 falsified (see sibling commits).

## Remaining work

1. **@doc-check coverage** — extend to 005, 007 x2, 008, 009, 010, 011, 012 x2, or record why a doc is exempt. Make the gate print coverage.
2. **Duplicate ADR numbers.** Two 007s (007-secretless-local-proxy = the decision, 007-secretless-plan = the plan) and two 012s (012-sender-constrained-oidc, Proposed; 012-vault-retirement, Accepted). Not renumbered here on purpose: cloister and other repos link to these paths, so renumbering is a cross-repo change and the user's call. Cheapest fix is probably renumbering the Proposed 012 to the next free number, since nothing depends on a Proposed ADR.
3. **012-sender-constrained-oidc has no bead** — its Bead line says "file when rsry reaches notme", which has long since happened.
4. **ADR-006 cites notme.bot-2b0d41** — a pre-rename repo prefix that resolves to nothing under either prefix. Either remap or drop.
5. **ADR-016 has no Bead line.** It generalizes 014/015 and was prompted by cloister review; may legitimately have no bead, but should say so rather than omit the field.

## Verification caveat worth recording

.beads/beads.jsonl is a STALE export. An initial pass over it flagged notme-7c7f83 (ADR-005) and notme-2bba44 (ADR-013) as dangling; both resolve fine against the live Dolt store — 7c7f83 is done, 2bba44 is legitimately open pending the rig change. Any ADR-to-bead reconciliation must query the live store, not the jsonl. This is the same lag that made scripts/bead-ref-check.ts warn rather than fail.

## Genuine code-vs-doc gap found

007-secretless-local-proxy's headline claim is STILL TRUE for the CF edge deployment: signing-authority.ts exports the CA private JWK and JSON.stringify's it into DO SQLite in persistent mode. Ephemeral (workerd) mode is fixed with extractable:false. The doc having no Status line meant nothing indicated whether this was solved. Tracked by notme-ae3130.
acceptance_criteria: `task docs:check` reports coverage (docs checked / docs total) rather than a bare claim count, and every docs/design/*.md either carries @doc-check or an explicit opt-out reason. Duplicate ADR numbers 007 and 012 resolved. No ADR lacks a Status line.

title: CA master + delegated JWT private keys are plaintext JWK in DO SQLite, while cloister's vault envelope-encrypts — root weaker than leaves
description:
Found while checking whether the ADR audit misaligns with cloister/vault after the ADR-012 vault lift. It does, and the direction is the wrong one.

## The asymmetry

cloister/vault (ADR-0030 §A3, lifted OUT of notme) does full envelope encryption:
- KEK derived from a Worker secret via HKDF (vault/src/kek-source.ts)
- random per-encrypt AES-256-GCM DEK; KEK wraps the DEK (vault/src/crypto.ts)
- sealed blob = {wrappedDek, iv, ciphertext}
- three-tier scoping with per-tenant HKDF info string "cloister/cred-iso/v1/tenant/<name>", so different tenantName means independent KEK (vault/src/kek-scope.ts)

notme's SigningAuthority DO does none of it:

    CREATE TABLE keys (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, private_jwk TEXT NOT NULL, ...)
    INSERT INTO keys (...) VALUES ('authority', JSON.stringify(privateJwk), ...)

The CA master Ed25519 private key is stored as a plaintext JWK. grep confirms nothing encrypts private_jwk anywhere in worker/src.

## Blast radius is inverted

- cloister vault compromise: tenant credentials, header values. Bad, scoped, per-tenant KEKs limit it.
- notme CA master key compromise: mint a cert for ANY identity with ANY scopes; forge at+jwt access tokens that every notme resource server accepts (ADR-015 records that verifyAccessToken leaves issuer unchecked by default); sign CA bundles; sign Interlace receipts.

The substrate encrypted the leaves and left the root in the clear. The key with the largest blast radius has the weakest storage.

## notme's own stated standard fails

007-secretless-local-proxy: "A system that claims to be secretless cannot have `cat *.sqlite | strings | grep '\"d\"'` extract the CA key." That is exactly the current persistent-mode state.

## It is a KNOWN unimplemented design, not an oversight

platform.ts validateKeyStorageConfig throws for mode "encrypted": "encrypted key storage is not yet implemented ... Fail hard so operators don't get a false sense of security." Failing closed is the right call and deserves credit — but it means production runs cf-managed with the key in cleartext.

## ADR-015 inherited it

delegated_jwt_keys (issuer, private_jwk TEXT NOT NULL, ...) — the per-issuer delegated signing keys added for ADR-015 in this same session go into the same plaintext table. The separate-key control that ADR-015 relies on still holds cryptographically (a delegated token cannot verify against notme's JWKS), but at-rest both keys are equally exposed.

## Why this is now cheap

Two working implementations of the exact pattern already exist in the org:
- cloister/vault/src/crypto.ts + kek-source.ts — the envelope + KEK rails, same runtime (Workers + DO + Web Crypto)
- notme's own worker/src/auth/dpop-nonce.ts — HKDF key derivation from a Worker secret under a domain separator, shipped and tested

So this is wiring an established in-org pattern into signing-authority.ts, not new crypto design.

## Threat-model caveat, stated honestly

The `cat *.sqlite` attack is most direct against local/workerd, and that path is ALREADY fixed — ephemeral mode uses extractable:false and stores an empty private_jwk. On the CF edge, DO SQLite is CF-managed and an attacker with Worker execution could sign regardless. What envelope encryption buys is separating "can read DO storage" from "can read Worker secrets" — two different compromise surfaces. That separation is precisely what cloister judged worth building, and notme holds the more valuable key.

Related: notme-ae3130 (007 Platform interface differs from implementation) is about the interface, not key-at-rest — different bead.
acceptance_criteria: Persistent-mode private keys (keys.private_jwk and delegated_jwt_keys.private_jwk) are envelope-encrypted at rest with a KEK derived from a Worker secret, matching cloister/vault/src/crypto.ts. validateKeyStorageConfig no longer throws for mode "encrypted". A test asserts the stored column does not contain the JWK "d" parameter in cleartext. `task worker:check` green.

title: Adopt leyline-mcp-descriptor for server.json once it supports multi-package producers
description:
Follow-on to notme-83706a. Blocked on `ley-line-open-44cc45`.

notme's `server.json` is hand-written and `scripts/check-image-versions.ts`
hand-implements the ADR-0041 §2 invariant. ley-line-open ships
`leyline-mcp-descriptor`, whose stated purpose is "Shared by every ART producer
so the coverage invariants are not reimplemented per repo" — but it cannot
represent notme today:

- singular `oci_image` / `oci_version`; notme publishes **two** images
- `transport_type` / `transport_url` required, and tool/group coverage
  validated; notme has no MCP surface at all

Neither is it published to crates.io, and adoption across the ecosystem is
currently zero (checked 2026-07-28), so nothing is lost by waiting.

## When ley-line-open-44cc45 lands

1. Replace the hand-written `server.json` with generated output, keeping the
   `_meta.art.cloister/v1` bundle block (notme-identity + notme-proxy tiers and
   rationale) — that content is notme's, not derivable.
2. Fold `scripts/check-image-versions.ts` down to whatever the descriptor does
   not cover. Two checks are notme-specific and likely stay regardless:
   - melange recipe versions track the tag, including the apk `-` → `_`
     spelling (apk reserves `-r<N>`, so `0.1.0-rc1` must be written
     `0.1.0_rc1` — melange rejects the former outright)
   - assertion against the *pushed* `VERSION`, shared with `image:publish`
3. Add a `gen:server-json:check` drift gate to CI, mirroring ley-line-open's.

Worth weighing at that point: adopting means a Rust build dependency in a repo
whose tooling is otherwise TS/JS (`scripts/*.ts` via tsx). If the descriptor
stays unpublished and must be built from a path/git dep, the duplication may
still be the cheaper trade — decide on the evidence then, not now.

## Do not lose

Whatever happens, the two ADR-0041 halves must stay enforced together: reject a
tagged/digest-pinned identifier AND reject an absent version. ley-line-open
v0.11.2 shipped through a guard that did only the first.

comments.text:
RESOLVED as acceptance option (b) — adoption rejected, with the measured
reason recorded rather than assumed.

The blocking dependency did land: `ley-line-open-44cc45` (multi-package) and
`ley-line-open-0135fa` (artifact-only mode) are both done, shipped in v0.13.0
as SHA256SUMS-verified per-platform binaries. So this was genuinely decidable
today, and I decided it on evidence from running the thing.

## What running the emitter showed

Fed it a notme descriptor. Its rendered output has no `title`, no
`websiteUrl`, and `_meta` is a closed two-field struct. Generating notme's
file would drop five things:

  1. `title`
  2. `websiteUrl`
  3. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/surface"`
  4. `_meta."io.github.agentic-research.notme/packages"`
  5. `_meta."art.cloister/v1".bundles[]`

(5) is the one that decides it, and it is worse than "not supported": the
crate uses that SAME `art.cloister/v1` key for tool-group claims, and omits
the key entirely when there are no groups. notme has no groups — so a
generated file drops ~40 lines of hypervisor-tier bundle topology
(ADR-0011/0018/0005) SILENTLY rather than erroring. This bead's own item 1
anticipated needing to keep that block; the emitter has no slot for it.

Secondary, both as predicted here: the crate is still not on crates.io (the
publish queue is staged pending an explicit go), and its own docs say "This
input shape WILL change" re: the transport scalars.

## What was adopted anyway — the part that mattered

The SHAPE, which is the actual interop surface. notme's `artifacts` array is
byte-identical to the emitter's rendered output, diff-verified:

    diff <(jq -S '._meta["io.modelcontextprotocol.registry/publisher-provided"]' llo-rendered.json) \
         <(jq -S '...' server.json)   -> IDENTICAL

So notme is conformant without being coupled, and a Rust build dependency
stays out of a TS/JS repo — the trade this bead flagged as worth weighing.

## "Do not lose" — kept, and extended

Both ADR-0041 halves still enforced together (absent version fatal, tagged
identifier fatal, per-entry). Item 3's drift gate landed as `task server:check`
on every PR. And the two notme-specific checks this bead predicted would stay
regardless did stay: the apk `-` → `_` recipe spelling, and the assertion
against the pushed `VERSION`.

Re-open if the descriptor grows an arbitrary-`_meta` passthrough — that single
change would flip this decision, since everything else already lines up.

Detail in notme-38044e. Closing.

title: SigningAuthority.generateBundle() drops prevKeyId — rotation grace period broken
description:
Discovered 2026-05-10 during Copilot review on PR #10 (CBOR canonical). Pre-existing bug; not caused by the CBOR work, but adjacent enough that the review caught it.

## The hole

`worker/src/signing-authority.ts:418-451` `generateBundle()`:

```ts
const bundle: Omit<CABundle, "signature"> & { signature?: string } = {
  epoch,
  seqno,
  keys: { [keyId]: pubKeyB64 },
  keyId,
  issuedAt: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
};
```

The bundle is built without a `prevKeyId` field.

`rotate()` at line 455-475 explicitly stores prevKeyId for the rotation grace window:

```ts
// Store prevKeyId for the transition window
await this.ctx.storage.put("prevKeyId", oldKeyId);
```

But `generateBundle()` never reads it back. Consequence:

- After a CA key rotation, the freshly signed CABundle has only the new keyId, not the previous one.
- Tokens issued under the old key get rejected with `unknown_key` immediately after rotation, even though the rotation grace window is supposed to keep them valid until they expire.
- The grace-window code in `revocation.ts::checkRevocation` (which checks `bundle.prevKeyId` for grace acceptance) has nothing to find.

## Why CBOR work didn't break this

The CBOR canonical encoder in `bundleCanonical()` correctly handles `bundle.prevKeyId ?? ""` — emitting the empty-string CBOR value when prevKeyId is absent. Cross-runtime byte equality with signet's Go-side `bundle.PrevKeyID string` (zero-value `""`) holds. So this bug is invisible to CBOR alignment tests; it's a separate functional bug.

## Fix

`generateBundle()` should read prevKeyId from DO storage (or from the same SQL state row) and include it:

```ts
const prevKeyId = (await this.ctx.storage.get<string>("prevKeyId")) ?? "";
const bundle: Omit<CABundle, "signature"> & { signature?: string } = {
  epoch,
  seqno,
  keys: { [keyId]: pubKeyB64, ...(prevKeyId ? { /* if grace-period public key still trusted */ } : {}) },
  keyId,
  prevKeyId,
  issuedAt: Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000),
};
```

Question for the implementer: should the `keys` map also include the previous key's public bytes during the grace window? Currently `keys` is single-key (current keyId only). For grace-period token verification to work, the verifier needs the previous public key in the bundle's `keys` map too. Need to look at `revocation.ts::checkRevocation` flow to confirm.

## Acceptance

- After `rotate()`, the next `generateBundle()` includes `prevKeyId` (and possibly the previous public key in `keys`).
- A test that rotates the key, regenerates the bundle, then verifies a token signed under the OLD key passes (during grace period).
- Worker test suite stays green.

## Anchors

- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:418-451` — generateBundle (the hole)
- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:455-475` — rotate (stores prevKeyId)
- `worker/src/revocation.ts::checkRevocation` — verifier that reads bundle.prevKeyId
- Copilot review on PR #10 (now closed; finding to be re-surfaced in the replacement PR)

comments.text: FIXED — PR #33 merged. rotate() now captures the old PUBLIC key before deleting it (stores prevKeyId + prevPubKey); generateBundle() republishes both (prev key in the signed keys map + prevKeyId), so old-key tokens verify through their grace window. Verified by typecheck + full suite (329). GAP: no dedicated rotation-grace regression test — SigningAuthority lacks a real-DO (runInDurableObject) test harness; filed as a follow-up.

title: notme: HIGH — /connections missing OIDC audience check enables account-link hijacking
description:
worker/worker.ts:1269 calls `verifyProof(body.proof, caKey)` with no `expectedAudience`. Sister endpoints `/join` (line 1380) and `/auth/oidc/login` (line 1423) both pass `"notme.bot"`. The omission breaks the same confused-deputy defense that verify-proof.ts:80-82 documents.

**Attack:**
1. Attacker authenticates to notme via passkey (principal-A).
2. Attacker obtains a Google OIDC token signed for the legitimate user `victim@gmail.com`, audience=evil-app.com (acquired via any means — public service exposure, shared XSS, etc.).
3. Attacker POSTs to /connections with their notme session + the stolen token. notme verifies signature OK, issuer trusted, **no audience check**, and stores `(google, victim@gmail.com) → principal-A` in the federated_identities table.
4. When the victim later tries to sign in to notme via Google for the first time (audience=notme.bot), `findPrincipalByOIDC` resolves to **principal-A** (the attacker's), not a fresh principal. The victim is silently routed into the attacker's notme account.

**Fix:** pass `"notme.bot"` as the `expectedAudience` argument to `verifyProof` at worker.ts:1269. Behavior matches /join and /auth/oidc/login.

**Test:** add a /connections test that submits an OIDC token with audience != notme.bot and asserts 401.

Threat model: belongs in the `auth.notme.bot` table as `oidc.connections.audience-binding`.

Fixed in commit eb70e78 (pushed to origin/main).

worker.ts:1269 now passes "notme.bot" as the expectedAudience argument to verifyProof, matching the existing pattern at /auth/oidc/login (line 1423) and /join (line 1380).

6 new tests in worker/src/__tests__/verify-proof.test.ts cover both the direct verifyOIDC path and the verifyProof dispatcher. THREAT_MODEL.md gained a new section 1b "OIDC connection / sign-in" with three rows (audience confused-deputy, token expiry ordering, issuer spoofing).

title: notme-proxy: add UDS-dial path on X-Cloister-Transport: uds header (companion role for cloister)
description:
Filed 2026-05-10 from `cloister-46fc1a` (closed) which wired cloister's `udsForward` backend to call out via the companion-proxy seam.

## Context

`notme-proxy` is the Rust mTLS forward proxy at `notme/proxy/`. Today it holds bridge cert + private key in process memory and presents mTLS on outbound TLS handshakes to external upstreams. Workerd Workers `fetch()` it via plain HTTP-on-loopback because workerd can't do TLS client auth from JS.

cloister also calls notme-proxy "cloister-companion" (per ADR-0005 in cloister) — same binary, two names. ADR-0005's design has the companion as the IPC seam for any wire workerd can't do directly: outbound mTLS today, **UDS-to-sibling-bundle** is the new use case as of `cloister-46fc1a`.

## What needs to happen

cloister-router now POSTs capnp ToolCall messages to notme-proxy with two new transport-indicator headers:

```
X-Cloister-Transport: uds
X-Cloister-Socket-Path: /run/cloister-uds/<bundle>.sock
```

The proxy should detect those headers and route via `AF_UNIX` connect → socket read/write → return the response bytes — instead of the existing mTLS-outbound path. Default (no header) keeps the existing mTLS behavior.

## Reference implementation

`scripts/stub-companion.mjs` in cloister already implements this proxy shape in Node for local dev:

- Reads `X-Cloister-Transport` header
- If `uds`: connects `AF_UNIX` to `X-Cloister-Socket-Path`, writes the request body, half-closes the write side, reads response bytes, returns verbatim
- If unset / `mtls`: keeps the existing mTLS-outbound behavior

The Rust impl should mirror that shape. tokio's `UnixStream` is the equivalent of node's `net.createConnection({path})`.

## Acceptance

- `notme-proxy` recognizes `X-Cloister-Transport: uds` + `X-Cloister-Socket-Path: <path>` headers.
- For UDS requests: opens `UnixStream`, write-half-closes after the request body, reads the response bytes, returns them in the HTTP response body. Status code mirrors success (200) / failure (502).
- Mounting: cloister's `cluster.compose.yaml` already declares the shared `cloister-uds:/run/cloister-uds` volume on the existing bundles. notme-proxy (when added to the topology as a sibling bundle in Phase 2B) inherits the same mount via `transport = (uds = void)` wire declarations; `scripts/emit-compose.mjs` handles it.
- Round-trip tests against the same fixtures cloister's `scripts/stub-companion.mjs` uses (or equivalent — TypeScript fixtures live in `cloister/test/manifest/uds-forward-backend.test.ts`).
- README updated to note the new transport path.

## Cross-repo cleanup

- cloister's `cloister-4cdba5` (closed; was filed pointing at a phantom future repo) → this bead.
- cloister's `docs/adr/0005-internal-wire-leyline-net.md` references "cloister-companion" — keep that name in cloister docs to match its terminology; just note in notme-proxy's README that the two names refer to the same binary.
- cloister's `docs/deployment/cluster-in-a-pod.md` already has the operator-facing explanation of the companion proxy role (per `cloister-46fc1a`); should still be accurate once this bead lands.

## Refs

- `cloister-46fc1a` (closed) — cloister side, wired the udsForward backend
- cloister `docs/adr/0005-internal-wire-leyline-net.md` — wire contract
- `notme/proxy/README.md` — existing mTLS forward proxy design
- cloister `scripts/stub-companion.mjs` — Node stub the Rust impl should mirror

comments.text:
Landed locally on main (3 commits, not pushed — awaiting human review):

- `52d8505` — handler + validation + tests
- `23a0f15` — apko `/run/cloister-uds/` mount point
- `45b7f42` — README docs (transport modes, sequence diagram, two-plane update)

## Implementation notes

**Framework**: notme-proxy is hyper 1 directly (no axum/tower) — service_fn + http1::Builder::serve_connection. Wired the header-based dispatch into a new `dispatch()` fn that branches on `X-Cloister-Transport` before either `handle_proxy` (existing mTLS, default) or `handle_uds` (new). Unknown transport values are rejected with 400 rather than silently falling through to mTLS, so a typo can't send a request across the wrong wire.

**Path validation** (security-critical): rejects on prefix mismatch (default `/run/cloister-uds/`, configurable via `NOTME_UDS_PREFIX`), any `..` path component, control characters (NUL/CR/LF/etc), and basenames that don't match `^[a-z0-9_-]+\.sock$`. Deliberately did NOT canonicalize via `fs::canonicalize` — that resolves symlinks and could expose paths the operator wired up intentionally as indirection. Literal prefix-match on the header value is the stronger contract.

**No tricky unicode cases**: `char::is_control()` covers the standard set; the lowercase `[a-z0-9_-]` regex on the basename closes the door on unicode lookalikes in the sock name. The header is UTF-8 (per HTTP), but the validation rules never look at the visual form — only bytes.

**Half-close**: `tokio::net::UnixStream` + `AsyncWriteExt::shutdown()` worked cleanly — sends FIN on the write half exactly as Node's `socket.end()` does. Mirrors the contract `proxyToUds` in cloister's `scripts/stub-companion.mjs`.

**Tests**: 11 → 26. New coverage:
- 9 unit tests for `validate_uds_path` and `is_valid_sock_name` (each rule has a positive + negative test)
- 1 test for `uds_prefix()` env-var handling
- 5 integration tests: spin up a real `UnixListener` + a real HTTP server on a per-test UDS, send raw HTTP/1.1 over an `AF_UNIX` client, assert proxy returns upstream bytes verbatim / 400 on malformed path / 502 on connect failure

**Cross-repo note**: the stub-companion's contract was a clean mirror — no divergence. One small thing: the stub doesn't time out on a stuck peer, but the Rust impl does (30s). That's an improvement, not a contract divergence. The header names + dispatch shape match exactly.

`task proxy:check` green (cargo build + 26 tests + clippy -D warnings). `task worker:check` still 23/338 (unchanged).

Bead remains open per instructions. Pre-push review-ready.
comments.author: rsry-mcp

comments.text:
Landed and pushed (`52d8505`, `23a0f15`, `45b7f42` on origin/main).

**Validation gate**:
- `task proxy:check`: 26 tests pass (was 11; +15 across unit + integration), clippy `-D warnings` clean
- `task worker:check`: 23 files / 338 tests, no regression

**Notable design choices the agent made that are worth knowing**:

1. **No `fs::canonicalize`** — symlink resolution would mask operator-intended indirection. Instead: literal prefix-match on header bytes + `Path::Component::ParentDir` check anywhere in the path. Catches `/run/cloister-uds/../etc/passwd` even though it starts with the right prefix.
2. **Fail-closed on unknown `X-Cloister-Transport` values** — 400, not silent fallthrough to mTLS. A typo'd header doesn't accidentally route to the existing path.
3. **30s read timeout on upstream** — additive safety over the cloister `stub-companion.mjs` reference: if a peer accepts but never writes back, the proxy returns 502 instead of hanging the request. The stub just hangs.

**Cloister-side unblock**: `cloister-b23309` (the Tier 2 integration bead for end-to-end `bead_create` through the cluster topology) had `depends_on: notme-58cc3e` and now becomes actionable. The companion is the real Rust proxy with UDS dial; cluster.compose.yaml's topology can grow companion as a fifth sibling bundle and the integration matrix can exercise the full chain.

**Closing** — the work matches the bead's scope + acceptance, tests pass, docs landed.

title: notme: P2 — /authorize/token missing audience allowlist (consistency)
description:
worker/worker.ts:1620 (/authorize/token) accepts any audience string from the request body and mints a Bearer token with it. /token at line 1666 enforces an `ALLOWED_AUDIENCES` set (rosary.bot, mcp.rosary.bot, auth.notme.bot, notme.bot, mache.rosary.bot); /authorize/token only checks `!audience`.

Practical impact is limited:
1. Session cookie is SameSite=Strict so cross-site POST is blocked
2. The /authorize redirect endpoint enforces ALLOWED_REDIRECT_HOSTS so the issued token can't be exfiltrated to attacker domains via that flow
3. Resource servers MUST validate audience anyway

But the inconsistency is real defense-in-depth gap: a session-authenticated user can request tokens for arbitrary audiences. Fix is to extract the allowlist constant and check it in both places.

Fix:
- Hoist ALLOWED_AUDIENCES out of the /token handler into a module-scope constant
- Apply the same `if (!ALLOWED_AUDIENCES.has(audience))` guard in /authorize/token
- Add a route test that confirms /authorize/token rejects audience="evil.example"

title: EPIC: DO alarm-loop hardening — post 'Cautionary tale' incident review (2026-05-10)
description:
Triggered by reddit cautionary tale (r/CloudFlare, 24 days before 2026-05-10) — operator hit 20 trillion DO reads on a single invoice from a runaway alarm loop. Their pattern:
- `onStart()` called `setAlarm()` without first checking `getAlarm()` → alarms compounded across instances
- 60+ preview deployments each spinning up their own DO populations multiplied the blast radius
- No spending cap on DOs in CF; the issue surfaced at invoice time

## notme audit verdict (2026-05-10)

**Not vulnerable to the redditor's specific bug.** `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:755-758` `scheduleNextRefresh()` correctly checks `getAlarm()` before `setAlarm()` — the exact fix the redditor wished he'd had. Single DO instance per deploy (`idFromName("default")`). No `onStart()` override. `RevocationAuthority` has no alarm at all.

**But 4 hardening opportunities stand:**

1. **(P1) `notme-XXX` — `alarm()` re-arm doesn't check `getAlarm()` first** (`signing-authority.ts:774`). CF's contract says one fire = one execution, so this is the canonical pattern, but defense-in-depth costs nothing and protects against runtime quirks.
2. **(P1) `notme-XXX` — No circuit breaker on consecutive failures.** The `try/catch` swallows errors and re-arms anyway. If `generateBundle()` fails repeatedly, we fire forever, each time doing real DO work. Need: track consecutive failures in storage; stop re-arming after N (loud log + escalation).
3. **(P2) `notme-XXX` — No fire counter / DO-internal observability.** Worker-level metrics (per `[observability] enabled = true`) don't show DO alarm fire counts.
4. **(P3) `notme-XXX` — Preview deployment exposure.** Currently `workers_dev = false` so no preview-deploys exist. But IF preview infrastructure ever lands, each preview = its own SigningAuthority DO = its own 4-min loop. 60+ previews = 900 fires/hour. The redditor's exact escalation mode.

## Constellation scope

**Audited: only notme has this exposure.** cloister has DOs (BlobStore, BeadStore) but no `setAlarm`/`getAlarm`/`alarm()` anywhere. cloister/vault has no DOs at all (the lifted vault code from notme didn't include the alarm-bearing SigningAuthority). No cross-repo beads needed.

## Implementation sequence

After PR #11 (CBOR canonical) merges → checkout main → pull → branch → fix the P1 + P2 beads in one mass-fix PR. Tier-1 patch sketched in conversation 2026-05-10 (defense-in-depth getAlarm + alarm_health table tracking failure_count + circuit breaker at 5 consecutive failures + reset RPC + getAlarmHealth RPC).

## Anchors

- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:31-79` — DO class definition (no onStart override; constructor inherits from base)
- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:197` — `scheduleNextRefresh()` call in getOrCreateSigningKey (✓ idempotent via getAlarm check)
- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:754-759` — `scheduleNextRefresh()` (the protective pattern)
- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:761-775` — `alarm()` (the unconditional re-arm at line 774)

- Adjacent: `notme-ae81c9` (passkey_challenges grows unbounded — another DO unbounded-growth concern; same defense-in-depth class)

title: DO hardening 3/4: alarm fire counter + getAlarmHealth RPC for observability
description:
Part of the DO alarm-loop hardening thread (parent epic filed alongside).

## Why

CF Workers have `[observability] enabled = true` which gives Worker-level metrics (request count, CPU time, errors). But it does NOT show DO-internal alarm fire counts. If a runaway alarm loop ever started — say, from a future CF runtime quirk or an unforeseen interaction with new code — the only signal would be the CF invoice (the redditor's situation, which cost 20 trillion DO reads).

Goal: a cheap, queryable counter of alarm fires + last-fire timestamp + last-outcome that operators can poll without scraping logs.

## Fix

Builds on the `alarm_health` table introduced by the circuit-breaker bead (sibling). Add columns:

```sql
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS alarm_health (
  id              TEXT PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT 'authority',
  failure_count   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  total_fires     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_fire_at    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,  -- Unix ms
  last_outcome    TEXT    NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  first_fire_at   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0   -- when this DO started firing
);
```

Increment `total_fires` at top of `alarm()`. Set `first_fire_at` if 0.

Add a DO RPC method:

```ts
async getAlarmHealth(): Promise<{
  totalFires: number;
  failureCount: number;
  lastFireAt: number;
  lastOutcome: string;
  firstFireAt: number;
  firesPerHour: number;  // total_fires / ((now - first_fire_at) / 3_600_000)
  expectedFiresPerHour: 15;  // 60min / 4min refresh
  driftRatio: number;        // firesPerHour / expectedFiresPerHour
}> { … }
```

Optionally expose via a Worker route (auth-gated, e.g. requires `authorityManage` scope):

```
GET /admin/do-health → { signingAuthority: getAlarmHealth() }
```

The `driftRatio` is the runaway detector. Expected = 15 fires/hour. If we see 30+/hour, something is double-firing.

## Acceptance

- `alarm_health.total_fires` increments on every fire.
- `getAlarmHealth()` returns the current state including `driftRatio`.
- A test that fires alarm() 10 times in succession asserts `total_fires == 10` and `driftRatio` is bounded.
- Optional: route `/admin/do-health` returns the health JSON, gated by `authorityManage`.

## Out of scope

- External-system alerting (PagerDuty, Slack webhook, CF email-on-spike) — operator concern, separate bead if needed.
- Cross-DO health aggregation (just SigningAuthority for now; RevocationAuthority has no alarm).

## Anchors

- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:761-775` — alarm() (where the counter lives)
- Sibling bead: circuit breaker (introduces alarm_health table; this bead extends the schema)
- Parent epic: filed alongside this
- `worker/wrangler.toml.example` — `[observability] enabled = true` (CF-level metrics; this bead complements at DO level)

comments.text:
**Done in PR #12 (commit `cf4901f` on main).**

`alarm_health` table tracks `failure_count`, `total_fires`, `last_fire_at`, `last_outcome`, `first_fire_at`. New `getAlarmHealth()` RPC returns the row plus derived `firesPerHour`, `expectedFiresPerHour`, `driftRatio`, `warmupComplete`, `circuitBreakerOpen`.

driftRatio is the runaway smoking gun — but only after warmup. Round-2 Copilot review caught that startup noise made `driftRatio > 1` ambiguous; fixed by adding `warmupComplete: boolean` (true when `total_fires >= DRIFT_RATIO_WARMUP_FIRES = 3`, ~12 minutes of cadence-paced data). Consumers must gate runaway alerts on `warmupComplete === true` before treating elevated driftRatio as an anomaly. After warmup, sustained `driftRatio > 1.2` indicates the alarm is firing faster than the cadence prescribes.

THREAT_MODEL.md §3 row updated to specify the warmup-gated interpretation. worker/README.md `signing-authority.ts` row mentions the new RPCs.
