title: README sweep across worker-esque subdirs (worker/, proxy/, action/, wasm/, schema/, gen/, scripts/, packages/, docs/)
description:
Repo currently has exactly one README.md (top-level). Several subdirectories serve distinct runtime/purpose roles and need their own.

Skip `vault/` (being moved to cloister per session 2026-05-09).

## What lives where (audit 2026-05-09)

| Folder | Has README? | What it is | Why it needs one |
|---|---|---|---|
| `worker/` | ❌ | Cloudflare Worker — TS, runs at CF edge AND locally via workerd. DOs: SigningAuthority, RevocationAuthority. cert-authority.ts, cert-exchange.ts, revocation.ts. Includes `config.capnp` and `examples/config-colocated.capnp` for local workerd. | Same code, two runtimes (CF prod + local workerd). Newcomers can't tell which entrypoint maps to which. |
| `proxy/` | ❌ | Local proxy holding bridge cert in memory (per `project_secretless_proxy.md` memory). Distinct language/runtime from `worker/`. | Two-plane model: proxy is the local plane; worker is the edge plane. Relationship needs documenting. |
| `action/` | ❌ | GitHub Action surface. Third runtime path (GHA). | Reused by other repos via `notme/action@<sha>`; consumers need to know calling convention. |
| `wasm/` | ❌ | Empty slot for `leyline-sign` wasm32 artifact (per cloister ADR-0007 + `ley-line-c764c6`). | Empty-with-purpose; needs to say "what lands here, when, from where, why empty." |
| `gen/` | ❌ | Generated TS + Go from `schema/identity.capnp`. | "Don't edit; run codegen" — currently only the file header says this, not the directory. |
| `schema/` | ❌ | `.capnp` files — declared single source of truth for cross-lang types. Has `codegen/capnp-to-ts.ts`. | Most-misunderstood folder; needs schema-evolution rules + codegen invocation + the wire-format caveat from `notme-XXXXXX` (capnp canonical-encoding bug). |
| `scripts/` | ❌ | `doc-check.ts` etc. | Conventional. |
| `packages/` | ❌ | melange/apko output (sbom .spdx.json, .tar bundles). git status currently shows `packages/out/`, `packages/sbom-aarch64.spdx.json`, `packages/notme.tar` etc. — build artifacts. | What consumes these? What's gitignored vs committed? |
| `docs/` | ❌ | ADRs (`design/005-…009`). | Index of ADRs. |

## What each README should answer

(Tier-1 sections — keep tight, skim-friendly)

1. **What this directory is.** One sentence.
2. **What runtime / language.** Disambiguates from sibling dirs.
3. **Entry points.** Which file is `main`? Which is the deploy target?
4. **How to run / build locally.** Concrete commands.
5. **What it depends on.** Service bindings, env vars, sibling dirs, external repos.
6. **Where to look next.** Pointer to relevant ADR or design doc.

## Out of scope

- `vault/` — moving to cloister.
- `node_modules/`, `coverage/`, `_agent_log/` — generated/transient.
- Top-level `README.md` — already exists; touch only to add a "Repo layout" section if missing.

## Acceptance

- 9 new READMEs landed, one per subdir in the table above.
- Top-level README has a "Repo layout" section listing the 10 subdirs (+ vault flagged as moving).
- Cross-links work: schema/README.md links to the capnp wire-format bead; wasm/README.md links to ley-line-c764c6.

title: Publish the OCI image to ghcr — the build machinery exists, nothing pushes it
description:
Filed 2026-07-28 from cloister, where the absence shows up as an unresolvable
image reference.

## What exists

notme can already build its image:

    packages/apko-notme.yaml
    packages/melange-workerd.yaml
    packages/melange-notme-app.yaml
    Taskfile: image:keygen -> image:apk -> image

`task image` runs `apko build apko-notme.yaml notme:{{.TAG}} notme.tar` and
prints "load with: docker load < packages/notme.tar". So the output is a LOCAL
tarball. Nothing pushes it to a registry.

## Why cloister cares

cloister's cluster.toml declares notme as a bundle:

    [[bundles]] name = "notme-identity"
      [bundles.external] image = "notme:0.1.0"

That reference is ACCURATE — `notme:0.1.0` is exactly what `task image`
produces — but it is not fetchable. An operator deploying the cluster on a fresh
host cannot pull it, and a cross-repo dependency graph cannot resolve the edge
by anything but the bare name, which is a heuristic rather than an assertion.

Compare rosary, which publishes and is therefore resolvable exactly:

    rosary/.github/workflows/release.yml
      IMAGE_NAME: ghcr.io/${{ github.repository_owner }}/rosary
      on: push: tags: ['v*']

and declares it in its own server.json packages[].oci as
`ghcr.io/agentic-research/rosary`. mache and ley-line-open do the same.

ADR-0041 (cloister) states each backend repo publishes its own distroless image.
notme is the outlier, and notme-proxy — a separate Rust binary in `proxy/` —
has no image at all.

## Ask

1. A release workflow that pushes the apko output to
   `ghcr.io/agentic-research/notme` on tag. rosary's release.yml is a working
   template in the same org with the same shape.
2. The same for `proxy/` (notme-proxy), which cloister declares as a
   hypervisor-tier bundle and which currently has neither an image nor a build
   task.
3. Once published, declare it in a `server.json` `packages[].oci` entry the way
   rosary/mache/ley-line-open do, so consumers derive the identifier rather than
   being told it.

Cloister will registry-qualify its cluster.toml references once (1) and (2) land.
Doing it before then would assert a location that does not exist, which is worse
than the bare name it replaces.

comments.text:
Implemented on branch `notme-83706a/ghcr-image-publish` (commit d5f2cdf). Not yet
tagged — the images do not exist at ghcr until a `v*` tag is pushed, so the
acceptance criteria (`docker pull` from a clean host) is NOT yet met.

## What landed

- `.github/workflows/release.yml` — tag-gated on `v*`, two INDEPENDENT jobs
  (matrix over notme / notme-proxy). Not chained, per the rosary v0.5.0
  failure where a coupled flaky build skipped the image publish.
- `packages/melange-notme-proxy.yaml` + `packages/apko-notme-proxy.yaml` —
  notme-proxy had no image at all. The cross-compile sits OUTSIDE melange
  (cargo-zigbuild, static musl), matching both existing recipes: neither
  compiles anything, so emulation only runs `install` rather than a cargo
  build.
- `server.json` — new, with both `packages[].oci` entries per ADR-0041 §2
  (bare identifier, version = pushed tag). No `remotes`, and the file states
  why: notme is an identity authority, not an MCP server, so cloister falls
  through cleanly instead of generating backends for tools that don't exist.
  The repo's default-deny `.gitignore` needed an explicit `!server.json`.
- Taskfile: `proxy:build:cross`, `image:proxy:apk`, `image:proxy`,
  `version:check`, `image:publish:{notme,proxy}`. CI runs no image command the
  Taskfile doesn't own.

## Version convention

**The `v` is stripped** — `v0.1.0` publishes `:0.1.0`. Chosen because
cloister's cluster.toml already says `notme:0.1.0`, so registry-qualifying is
a prefix addition rather than a version rewrite.

`version:check` asserts `server.json` against **the tag the publish job
actually pushes**, sharing the `VERSION` variable with `image:publish` — not
against the git tag, which would pass while the registry 404s. Each entry is
checked independently (a correct notme + stale notme-proxy is reachable), and
an **absent** version is rejected as firmly as a wrong one — the half that
ley-line-open v0.11.2 shipped through.

Six failure modes verified to fail correctly: wrong version, absent version,
tag baked into identifier, deleted entry, raw `v`-prefixed input, recipe drift.

## Verified locally

- `proxy:build:cross` → static ELF for both x86_64 and aarch64 musl
- melange builds `notme-proxy-0.1.0-r0.apk`, binary at `/usr/bin/notme-proxy`
- apko assembles the image; container **runs and listens**:
  `notme-proxy: listening on tcp 0.0.0.0:1080`, port reachable from host
- existing `task image` still builds (the `ARCH`→`ARCHS` rename is compatible)
- `pin:check`, `docs:check`, `version:check`, `proxy:check` (27/27), and
  `actionlint` on all workflows: clean

## Blocker found and fixed

notme-proxy **panicked on every startup, on every target** — two rustls crypto
providers enabled. Filed as notme-76123b and fixed in 29c69e8. Publishing the
first-ever notme-proxy image would otherwise have satisfied `docker pull`
while shipping something that cannot start. Pre-existing; reproduced
identically on a native macOS build, so not a cross-compilation artifact.

## Not done — deliberately

Cloister's `cluster.toml` is untouched. Per this bead, cloister
registry-qualifies its own references after these are published.

## Next

Push the branch, merge, then tag `v0.1.0` to actually publish. Only then can
the acceptance criteria be verified by `docker pull` from a clean host.

comments.text:
**Published and verified.** Acceptance criteria met at `v0.1.0-rc3`
(run 30404303305, both jobs green).

```
ghcr.io/agentic-research/notme:0.1.0-rc3       @sha256:a5202a7e8e9b…
ghcr.io/agentic-research/notme-proxy:0.1.0-rc3 @sha256:55191e873db9…
```

Verified by pull from a clean local docker (images removed first, pulled
anonymously — both packages are public):

- `docker pull` succeeds for both, no auth
- multi-arch: both indexes list `linux/amd64` + `linux/arm64`
- `cosign verify` **by tag** succeeds for both, and the reported
  `docker-manifest-digest` equals the digest the publish job pushed — i.e. the
  signature is on the INDEX the tag resolves to, which is what the review fix
  corrected. Both an SBOM attestation (`spdx.dev/Document`) and a signature
  (`sigstore.dev/cosign/sign/v1`) are present
- `notme` boots and answers `GET /health` → **200**
- `notme-proxy` loads its cert, logs `listening on tcp 0.0.0.0:1080`, and
  accepts a connection

## It took three release candidates

Each failure was a path no local setup exercised, which is the whole argument
for the rc.

| tag | failed on |
|---|---|
| rc1 | `worker:build-local` — `@agentic-research/dpop` resolves to a gitignored `dist/` that only existed locally from an earlier build; `--ignore-scripts` is exactly what skips the prepack that would produce it. Plus `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` SHA-pinned without `toolchain:`, so it ran `rustup default ''` |
| rc2 | `bwrap not found on $PATH` — melange defaults to bubblewrap on Linux and GitHub's ubuntu runners don't ship it |
| rc3 | — green |

rc2's failure was the exact residual risk called out in the PR review. Fixed by
pinning `--runner docker` in the Taskfile rather than apt-installing a second
untested sandbox: docker is already a hard requirement here (apko,
`docker load`) and was the runner every local build was validated against, so
local and CI now take the same path.

Tags were never moved — each fix got a new rc. Nothing had published under rc1
or rc2 so re-pointing would have been safe, but this change set's premise is
that tags are immutable handles and the digest is the pin.

## Remaining

- `0.1.0` proper is a version bump away: `server.json` (both entries) to
  `0.1.0` and both melange recipes to `0.1.0`. The pipeline itself is now
  proven end to end.
- Cloister can registry-qualify and digest-pin once `0.1.0` is cut.
- Prereleases need two spellings — `0.1.0-rc3` in `server.json` (OCI tag),
  `0.1.0_rc3` in the melange recipes (apk reserves `-r` for the release
  suffix). `version:check` knows the mapping; see `packages/README.md`.

title: Signing oracle protocol in identity.capnp + OpenAPI projection
description:
Add SignRequest/SignResponse/PublicKeyResponse structs to identity.capnp for the signing oracle protocol (the wire format between agent and key holder).

Once mache-845144 lands, this schema projects to OpenAPI automatically. Until then, hand-maintain a minimal OpenAPI spec for /sign and /public-key.

The Go crypto.Signer wrapper is ~10 lines on top of the generated client. The signing oracle IS the unix primitive (ssh-agent pattern) that unifies the CA and proxy models.

title: SDK: Go verifier middleware — mTLS client cert → WIMSE identity
description:
Light verifier SDK for Go services. Loads CA cert from /.well-known/ca-bundle.pem, validates client certs on incoming mTLS, extracts WIMSE identity from SAN URI, makes identity available via context. ~100 lines.

Three deployment classes:
1. Library/middleware (this bead): import a package, 5 lines to integrate
2. Local user proxy: workerd sidecar holds certs, proxies with mTLS
3. Bastion/gateway: shared reverse proxy validates certs, forwards with identity headers

This is Class 3 from 008 spec — the service needs zero notme-specific code beyond the CA cert.

title: SDK: gRPC UnaryServerInterceptor for notme cert verification
description: gRPC interceptor that extracts client cert from TLS peer, validates against notme CA, extracts WIMSE identity. Same pattern as Go HTTP middleware but for gRPC.\n\nUsage: grpc.NewServer(grpc.UnaryInterceptor(notme.VerifyInterceptor(caCert)))

title: workerd: add mTlsCertificate binding for local mTLS outbound
description:
Root cause (5 why): workerd has no binding type for client certs in open-source. CF has mtls_certificates as a platform feature. The fix: add it to workerd's capnp schema + C++ implementation.

Scope:
1. Add mTlsCertificate to Worker.Binding union in workerd.capnp
2. Parse into kj::TlsContext with keypair
3. When fetch() sees cf.tlsClientAuth, pass keypair to KJ HTTP client
4. KJ uses it in SSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain + SSL_CTX_use_PrivateKey

For dynamic certs: file-watch (reload PEM on change) or JS API (env.CERT.update(pem, key)).

This is a C++ change to cloudflare/workerd. Could be upstream PR (benefits all standalone workerd users) or fork.

Makes local workerd + CF production use identical code: fetch(url, { cf: { tlsClientAuth: env.MY_CERT } })

comments.text:
PRIORITY QUESTION — the workaround this bead predates now ships as a signed,
published image. Assessed 2026-07-30 while looking for P0 work.

## What the bead asks for is still accurate

workerd genuinely has no client-cert binding in open source; `mtls_certificates`
is a CF platform feature. The four-step scope (capnp `Worker.Binding` union →
`kj::TlsContext` → `cf.tlsClientAuth` → `SSL_CTX_use_certificate_chain`) is a
correct description of the upstream change. Nothing here is wrong.

## But it is no longer the only path, and the alternative is done

notme-proxy exists precisely because of this gap — `docs/design/007-secretless-
local-proxy.md` says so directly ("the bridge cert needs a process boundary
workerd can't [provide]"). As of today it is not a plan:

    ghcr.io/agentic-research/notme-proxy:0.1.0
    sha256:4f55809ba44bdadb63db338e5c33a5b733b2aaa62c9d5de6600d8370be5c1b96

multi-arch, cosign-signed, SBOM-attested, boots from the published image, and
holds the bridge cert in process memory so no Worker ever touches the key. It
is a declared hypervisor-tier bundle in cloister's topology (ADR-0005 companion
role).

So the capability this bead unblocks is available. What the bead would buy is
narrower than "local mTLS outbound": it is **removing the extra process** and
making local workerd and CF production run byte-identical code
(`fetch(url, { cf: { tlsClientAuth: env.MY_CERT } })`). Real, but a
simplification rather than an enabler.

## Why that matters for P0

This is a C++ change to `cloudflare/workerd` — either an upstream PR with an
external review cycle we do not control, or a fork we then carry. Neither is
schedulable the way the label implies, and holding P0 on work that cannot be
started-and-finished here makes the priority signal less useful for everything
below it.

Recommend: **P2, retitled toward the actual benefit** — "collapse the
notme-proxy process by teaching workerd an mTlsCertificate binding" — with a
note that the two-plane model is the supported path meanwhile. Not
re-prioritising unilaterally; flagging because "2 open P0s" currently reads as
two urgent notme tasks and neither is one.

Worth keeping regardless: if it IS pursued, upstream-PR-not-fork is the right
call for the reason the description already gives — it benefits every
standalone workerd user, and a fork is a permanent carry.

title: Security: review remaining hypothesized vulnerabilities
description:
From session hypothesis list — not yet verified by either audit pass:

1. WebAuthn origin validation — does verifyRegistration/verifyAuthentication check exact origin or just hostname? RP ID mismatch attacks.
2. parseCookie defensiveness — malformed cookie headers, cookie injection via header manipulation
3. DPoP audience parameter — can caller mint tokens with arbitrary audience claims? Should audience be validated against an allowlist.
4. Clock skew on cert notBefore — window between DO signing time and verifier check time. Should allow small skew (30s).
5. DO SQLite parameterized queries — audit every .exec() call for string interpolation vs parameterized binding
6. Session HMAC entropy — btoa(String.fromCharCode(...crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)))) — is this actually 256 bits after base64 encoding?
7. No CORS policy on /token or /cert — any origin can POST
8. return_to parameter reflection — user-controlled path reflected in login redirect
9. Session revocation — no server-side store, stolen cookie = 24h access
10. Admission control — recovery key, multi-passkey requirement, time-delayed destructive ops (from step-ca research)

Each should be TDD: write the test that proves the vulnerability exists, then fix.

title: action/: dist/index.js stale — src has HTTPS enforcement that committed bundle is missing
description:
Discovered 2026-05-09 during README sweep agent dispatch.

## The drift

GitHub Actions consumers run `action/dist/index.js` directly (per `runs: node20, main: dist/index.js` in `action.yml`). GitHub does NOT execute `npm install` for action consumers — only the committed bundle.

`action/src/index.ts` was modified at commit `779ef60` to enforce HTTPS on `authority_url` (rejects `http://` unless localhost). This is a defensive guard against accidentally transmitting OIDC JWTs in plaintext.

**`action/dist/index.js` was last rebuilt at commit `f171e8d`, BEFORE `779ef60`.**

Consumers pinned to any tag/SHA after `779ef60` but before a fresh `dist/` rebuild are running an action that:
- Accepts non-HTTPS `authority_url`
- Will silently transmit the OIDC bearer token in plaintext if `authority_url` is `http://...` and not localhost

The pinned-by-SHA model assumes `dist/index.js` reflects `src/index.ts`. Drift breaks that assumption. Anyone reading the code thinks the guard is shipped; consumers are not actually getting it.

## Fix

```bash
cd action
npm install
npm run build      # esbuild src/index.ts → dist/index.js
git add dist/
git commit -m "[notme-XXXXXX] build(action): rebuild dist after HTTPS-enforcement change in src"
```

Then verify by reading the bundled output for the HTTPS check string.

## Prevention

Add a CI step that:
1. Runs `npm run build` in `action/`.
2. Fails if `git diff --exit-code dist/` shows any change post-build.

This is the standard "dist must match src" CI gate that GitHub's `actions/typescript-action` template uses. Without it, the next dist drift will land the same way.

## Adjacent finding (not a bead, just noting)

`octo_sts_scope` is declared as an input but the TS action just emits `core.warning` redirecting users to a separate reusable workflow — `github_token` output is always empty in the TS code path. This IS communicated via the warning, so it's a documented punt rather than a stealth bug. If you want to remove the redirect: separate bead.

## Anchors

- `action/src/index.ts` — current source
- `action/dist/index.js` — stale bundle
- `action/action.yml` — declares the entry point
- Commits: `779ef60` (src change), `f171e8d` (last dist rebuild)
- `.github/workflows/` — needs the dist-drift CI gate

comments.text:
**FALSE POSITIVE — closing.**

Verified 2026-05-09: ran `cd action && npm install && npm run build`. Output: `git diff --stat dist/index.js` returned empty. The committed `dist/index.js` is current.

The HTTPS guard string from `src/index.ts:66` ("authority_url must be HTTPS — an HTTP URL would transmit the OIDC token in plaintext") **IS** present in `dist/index.js` (grep -c = 1).

The action sub-agent that surfaced this finding compared `git log` timestamps incorrectly — both `f171e8d` shows up as the latest commit for src AND dist. The HTTPS-enforcement commit `779ef60` was committed alongside the dist rebuild, not after.

**Lesson:** verify agent findings with the actual rebuild, not just `git log` reading. Agents can read git correctly but mis-conclude.

The CI gate this bead recommended (fail PR if `git diff --exit-code dist/` after rebuild) is still a good idea — would have caught this verification dance and prevented the false alarm next time.

title: worker/ discovery drift: signet-authority.json advertises endpoints that don't exist (/exchange-token, /api/cert/register, /healthz)
description:
Discovered 2026-05-09 during README sweep agent dispatch.

## The drift

`worker/worker.ts` `/.well-known/signet-authority.json` returns a discovery doc that advertises:

- `exchange_token_endpoint = /exchange-token` — **route does not exist** in `worker.ts`
- `registration_endpoint = /api/cert/register` — **route does not exist** in `worker.ts`

A client (resource server, partner integration, third-party auditor) following the discovery doc to integrate against notme will hit 404s. This is the kind of mismatch that makes "well-known"-style discovery worse than no discovery at all — the consumer trusts the published doc.

## Two fixes (pick one)

**(A) Remove the dead advertisements.**
- Drop `exchange_token_endpoint` and `registration_endpoint` from the discovery JSON if those flows aren't shipping.
- Drop `/healthz` from the landing endpoints map.
- Cheaper. Honest about what's actually wired.

**(B) Wire up the advertised endpoints.**
- Implement `/exchange-token` (likely a pre-008 single-cert flow that was renamed to `/cert/gha`?)
- Implement `/api/cert/register` (purpose unclear from the doc alone — read git history for intent)
- Implement `/healthz` (trivial — just return `{"ok": true}`)
- More work; only justified if these endpoints have real consumers somewhere.

Most likely answer: (A). The discovery doc looks like it was written ahead of implementation and never trimmed.

## Acceptance

- `cd worker && npx tsx ../scripts/doc-check.ts` (or whatever the validation flow is) does NOT advertise endpoints that aren't implemented.
- Discovery JSON only lists routes that actually return non-404.
- Optional CI gate: a test that fetches every endpoint in `signet-authority.json` and asserts response status != 404.

- `worker/worker.ts` — discovery handler + the live route table
- `worker/public/` — landing JSON if relevant
- `scripts/doc-check.ts` — currently validates `@endpoints` claims in `worker.ts` only via `pathname === "..."` regex; the discovery JSON is a separate surface that this script doesn't check (per the `scripts/README.md` audit, doc-check has false-negative risk for non-inline route checks)

title: worker/: PASSKEY_LIMITER binding declared in wrangler but never read in code
description:
Discovered 2026-05-09 during README sweep agent dispatch.

## The drift

`worker/wrangler.toml.example` declares a rate-limit binding:

```toml
[[unsafe.bindings]]
name = "PASSKEY_LIMITER"
type = "ratelimit"
namespace_id = "..."
simple = { limit = 5, period = 60 }
```

(5 requests/minute cap.) But `env.PASSKEY_LIMITER` is **never accessed** in `worker.ts` or any `worker/src/*.ts` file. The binding is allocated but dormant.

## What this means in practice

Passkey register + login endpoints currently have no rate limit:
- `/auth/passkey/register/options`
- `/auth/passkey/register/verify`
- `/auth/passkey/login/options`
- `/auth/passkey/login/verify`

`CERT_LIMITER` and `TOKEN_LIMITER` ARE wired (used in `/cert/gha` and `/token` paths); only `PASSKEY_LIMITER` is dead. Either:

1. Wire it — wrap the four passkey routes with a `PASSKEY_LIMITER.limit({key: ...})` check before invoking the DO. The DO call is the expensive operation; rate-limiting at the edge protects the DO from passkey-flood DoS.
2. Remove it — drop the binding from wrangler.toml.example. Document the decision in worker/README.md.

(1) is the safer answer — the binding was clearly intended to throttle passkey enumeration / DoS attempts. Removing it leaves an attack vector open that the original author thought was worth addressing.

## Acceptance

- Either: `env.PASSKEY_LIMITER.limit({key})` is called in all four passkey routes before they hit the DO.
- Or: the binding is removed from `wrangler.toml.example` AND the rationale is captured in worker/README.md (so a future reader doesn't re-add it).
- Tests: a unit test that sends >5 requests/min to a passkey route gets 429s on requests 6+.

## Anchors

- `worker/wrangler.toml.example` — declares the binding
- `worker/worker.ts` `handlePasskey` — the callsite that should consume the limiter
- `worker/src/auth/dpop-handler.ts` and `worker/src/cert-exchange.ts` — examples of how the other limiters are wired (CERT_LIMITER, TOKEN_LIMITER)

title: vault: extend tsc scope to include vault/src — surfaces 8 hidden type errors
description:
Companion to ce2dbf4 (proxy CI integration) and the dormant-test activations. Vault tests run in vitest now, but `vault/src/*.ts` is still NOT included in any tsconfig. Worker's tsconfig only globs worker code; the SDK was added in this iteration's commit.

Attempting to extend `worker/tsconfig.json` to also include `../vault/src/**/*.ts` surfaces 8 real type errors that runtime tests don't catch:

1. `vault/src/crypto.ts:76, 84` — argument typed as `CryptoKey | CryptoKeyPair` passed where only `CryptoKey` accepted; needs narrowing or correct type at the callsite.
2. `vault/src/worker.ts:27, 31, 34, 37, 56, 82` — `DurableObjectStub<undefined>` doesn't know vault's RPC methods (`getCredential`, `putCredential`, `deleteCredential`, `listServices`, `checkAndStoreJti`, `proxyRequest`). Needs a typed binding (e.g. `DurableObjectNamespace<CredentialVault>` so the stub picks up the class's RPC surface).

Fix path:
- Type the env binding in vault/src/worker.ts as `DurableObjectNamespace<CredentialVault>` (TS 5.6+ supports the parameterized form per CF docs).
- In vault/src/crypto.ts, narrow the input type at the boundary so subtle.encrypt/decrypt sees `CryptoKey`.
- Re-extend `worker/tsconfig.json` include with `../vault/src/**/*.ts`.

Once green, vault is under the same tsc + vitest CI signal as the worker. This was deferred from this loop because fixing all 8 is more than the iteration's risk budget; tests still pass at runtime.

comments.text:
Partial progress in commit a879729 — the simpler of the two error categories is fixed in isolation:

- ✅ `vault/src/crypto.ts:65` — `subtle.generateKey({name:"AES-GCM",...})` cast to CryptoKey. Eliminates 2 of the 8 errors.

The DO-binding typing turned out trickier than the bead's recommendation suggested. Tried two paths:

1. **`Env.VAULT: DurableObjectNamespace<CredentialVault>` + `class CredentialVault extends DurableObject<Env>`** — TS rejects with `TS2589: Type instantiation is excessively deep and possibly infinite`. The cycle is Env → VAULT → CredentialVault → DurableObject<Env> → Env.

2. **`extends DurableObject` (unparameterized) + `DurableObjectNamespace<CredentialVault>`** — same TS2589. The cycle is shorter but still recursive (CredentialVault references Env via `private env: Env` for its constructor and methods that read env props).

Working approach for whoever takes this next:

- Extract a separate RPC-only interface (no Env reference): `interface CredentialVaultRpc extends Rpc.DurableObjectBranded { getCredential(...): ..; putCredential(...): ..; ... }`. Use it as the type parameter on DurableObjectNamespace.
- The class itself can `extends DurableObject` (if `cloudflare:workers` import works for vault's tsc context — needs verification by adding vault to tsconfig include).
- Or alternatively, wrap each `vault.<method>(...)` call site in a typed shim that the worker.ts uses, isolating the cast to one place.

There's also a Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> vs ArrayBuffer mismatch at crypto.ts:137 surfaced when vault is included in tsconfig — not present in the original 8 because tsc stops counting after a certain depth. Likely a `lib` config issue or an explicit `as ArrayBuffer` cast site.

Bead remains open. Risk budget for this loop iteration was the limiter — the recursion fight is worth a clean session, not a 5-minute slice.

title: DEFERRED: Remove notme/vault/ once cloister's copy is proven (no urgency)
description:
**Scope changed 2026-05-09**: deferred indefinitely. cloister-9ad9eb is now copy-not-move — cloister gets a self-contained AGPL-3 copy of vault/, notme keeps its Apache-2.0 copy unchanged. Consolidation only happens when there's a concrete reason (e.g. notme starts using cloister's vault via service binding, or vault grows in a way that makes maintaining two copies painful).

## When to revisit this bead

Trigger conditions (any one is sufficient):

1. **notme starts depending on cloister's vault** — service binding, npm dependency, or path-shared. At that point notme's local copy becomes redundant.
2. **Active divergence between the two copies** — bug fixes or features land in one but not the other. Either consolidate or accept the fork explicitly.
3. **External user asks** — "where's the canonical vault implementation?" If the answer is "either, but they might drift," that's a signal to pick one.
4. **License-strategy change** — if notme's Apache-2.0 posture changes, or if cloister's AGPL-3 needs to fan out to notme too.

## When NOT to do this

- "It feels duplicative." Two copies with clear ownership is fine; the cost is low and the coupling cost of a service binding is non-zero.
- "OSS readiness needs notme cleaned up too." cloister's OSS readiness doesn't depend on notme being touched. The cloister-side lift gives cloister everything it needs.

## Original scope (kept for reference, not active work)

If/when this bead reactivates, the original migration plan was:

- Delete `notme/vault/` directory.
- Remove `../vault/src/**/*.ts` from `notme/worker/tsconfig.json` `include`.
- Remove `../vault/src/__tests__/**/*.test.ts` from `notme/worker/vitest.config.ts` test paths.
- Decide on `notme/worker/THREAT_MODEL.md` (22 vault references) — move with the code OR leave a redirect.
- Update notme's top-level README.md if it references the vault sibling.

## Files (when reactivated)
- `vault/` (deletion)
- `worker/tsconfig.json` (edit)
- `worker/vitest.config.ts` (edit)
- `worker/THREAT_MODEL.md` (move or split)

title: Design: credential mint for bd Dolt sql-server MySQL auth (cloister-side substrate adoption)
description:
## Context

The rosary LLM (2026-06-23 session) flipped ADR-0012's read: `bd` ships with a socket-mode `dolt sql-server` that handles concurrent writers + is sandbox-friendly. The corrected substrate plan is for ALL bead consumers (rosary, cloister, claude code sessions) to speak MySQL to a shared bd-managed Dolt sql-server.

Cloister-side design lives in `cloister-9d19e3` (filed in cloister tracker 2026-06-23): cloister-router gets a service binding → external dolt-sql-server, with cloister mediating credentials via the existing ADR-0024 `cloister/credential-isolation/v1` path. This bead captures what notme has to ship for the credential mint.

## Question

Does the existing GHA-OIDC bridge cert path (`notme/action`, `pkg/oidc`, `LocalCA.IssueBridgeCert`) work for authenticating an agent identity to dolt-sql-server, OR does this need a new credential type?

## Likely answer (to be confirmed in design)

**MySQL doesn't natively understand bridge certs.** Two options:

### Option A — Vault stores a MySQL user/password; notme out of scope

- Operator pre-provisions a MySQL user on the dolt-sql-server
- The password lands in cloister's vault via `wrangler secret put` or kek-source
- Cloister vault DO injects `Authorization: Basic ...` or sets MySQL `Cleartext Plugin` on the connection
- **Notme work**: NONE. The credential is an operator-managed secret; notme doesn't touch it.

### Option B — TLS client cert, minted per agent identity

- Dolt-sql-server configured with `--require-secure-transport` + a CA bundle from notme
- Each agent identity gets a short-lived TLS client cert minted by notme's `LocalCA` (same path as GHA bridge certs)
- Dolt verifies the cert chain; agent identity = client cert CN/SAN
- **Notme work**: extend `LocalCA.IssueBridgeCert` to support a new `--purpose mysql-client` flag that issues with `extKeyUsage = clientAuth` and an appropriate SAN namespace. Add `/exchange-mysql-cert` endpoint analogous to `/exchange-token`.

### Option C — DPoP-style proof in a MySQL `connect_attrs` field

- Agent sends DPoP-shaped proof in the MySQL connection's `connect_attrs` map at handshake time
- Dolt-sql-server validates via a custom auth plugin (requires bd patching — likely OUT of scope)

## Scope of this bead

**Design + decision, not implementation.** Output:

1. Audit which MySQL auth shape dolt-sql-server actually supports (cleartext password, native_password, caching_sha2_password, TLS client cert via mysql_clear_password, etc.)
2. Choose A / B / C based on (a) what dolt-sql-server supports, (b) which keeps the trust-root posture clean, (c) which preserves the "credential never leaves vault" property
3. If A: file follow-up notme beads as `none` (nothing to do)
4. If B: file follow-up notme bead for `LocalCA` extension + new `/exchange-mysql-cert` endpoint
5. If C: file follow-up notme bead PLUS a bd-side bead for the custom auth plugin

## Trust-boundary considerations

- Whichever credential shape: it MUST live in cloister's vault, never in plaintext on the wire INTO the Worker
- Per ADR-0019 sign-helper precedent: prefer short-lived credentials minted on-demand over long-lived static secrets
- TLS client certs (Option B) have the cleanest "short-lived + non-bearer" properties — match the bridge-cert precedent

## Dependencies

- **Blocks on**: cloister-9d19e3 (cloister ADR-0033 for the dolt-sql-server binding) — that ADR picks the credential shape from the cloister side; this bead implements notme's side of that choice.
- **Indirectly blocks on**: rosary ADR-0012 rewrite (the substrate adoption decision)

## Tracking

- Parent: cloister-9d19e3 (cloister ADR-0033 design)
- Related notme work: existing GHA-OIDC bridge cert path (`pkg/oidc`, `LocalCA.IssueBridgeCert`, `/exchange-token`), bead `signet-882eca` (bridge cert with capability X.509 extensions — relevant precedent)
- Threat model touchpoint: notme adds a new attack-surface row for the mysql-client cert mint if Option B

title: Service bindings: split notme into public + private surfaces
description:
Use CF service bindings to eliminate public attack surface for internal operations.

Public surface (reachable via internet):
- Passkey login/register
- GHA OIDC cert exchange (/cert/gha)
- CA bundle (/.well-known/*)
- DPoP token endpoint (/token)

Private surface (only via service binding, no public URL):
- cert minting (mintBridgeCert RPC)
- admin operations (epoch rotation, bootstrap reset)
- principal management
- scope grants

Consuming Workers bind to notme-bot in wrangler.toml:
```toml
[[services]]
binding = "AUTH"
service = "notme-bot"
```

Then call directly: `env.AUTH.mintBridgeCert(subject, pubkey)`

This eliminates for internal calls:
- CORS (same-process)
- Audience validation (binding IS the auth)
- Rate limiting (trust the caller)
- Token/header auth (not needed)
- Public attack surface (endpoints not reachable)

The public surface still needs all the hardening. But the internal surface becomes zero-trust-by-architecture.

comments.text:
SUBSTANTIALLY BUILT already — assessed 2026-07-30 while looking for P0 work.
The split exists; what was missing was that its trust boundary did not hold.

## The private surface this bead asks for is present

`worker/worker.ts:72` — `export class AuthService extends WorkerEntrypoint`,
with the eight RPC methods the description calls for:

    mintBridgeCert   mintDPoPToken   getPublicKeyPem   getCACertificatePem
    getAuthorityState   verifySession   authenticate   proxy   sign   identity

`mintBridgeCert` is reachable ONLY by RPC — it is not in the public route
table. The public routes are the ones this bead lists as public (passkey
login/register, `/cert/gha`, `/.well-known/*`, `/token`) plus user-facing pages;
no route exposes epoch rotation, bootstrap reset, principal management or
scope grants. So items 1–4 of the private surface are done, and the
"eliminates CORS / audience validation / rate limiting / public reachability"
reasoning holds as written.

## What was NOT true: "the binding IS the auth"

That premise is the load-bearing one in this bead, and it was false in
practice. `authenticate()` accepted `identity`, `scopes` and `expiresAt` as
caller-supplied fields and assigned them verbatim — so the binding authorized
*reaching* AuthService but nothing constrained *who the caller claimed to be*
once through. `proxy()` then gated on those scopes and audit-logged that
identity.

Filed as notme-6ad276 and fixed today in PR #54: those three fields are gone
from the parameter type, and identity/scopes/expiry are derived from
CA-verified certs. Invariant now: entrypoint-DERIVED, never
entrypoint-RECEIVED.

That is the correction this bead's own model needed. "Zero-trust-by-
architecture for the internal surface" is only true if the entrypoint refuses
to take the caller's word for its principal; it now does.

## Remaining, if this bead stays open

The bead's `files` names only `worker/worker.ts` and it has no acceptance
criteria, which is why "is this done?" was not answerable from the bead alone.
Concrete residue worth either doing or explicitly dropping:

1. The wrangler.toml example in the description is not present as a tested
   contract anywhere — nothing asserts a consumer binding shape.
2. No test asserts the NEGATIVE half: that admin/rotation/principal-management
   operations are absent from the public fetch handler. That is the property
   this bead exists for, and it is currently true by construction rather than
   by assertion, so a future route addition could regress it silently.

Both are small. Suggest re-scoping this bead to (2) — a route-surface
assertion — since (1) belongs with whichever consumer actually binds AUTH.

Not closing unilaterally: P0 with no acceptance criteria and a description
that is mostly satisfied is exactly the shape that gets closed too early.

title: Expose getEpochPublicKey on ReceiptSigner — cloister can only archive epochs it happened to observe
description:
Found 2026-08-04 answering "who publishes the Interlace epoch index?".

OWNERSHIP, since it was unclear: publication is CLOISTER's and already built. `/.well-known/interlace/index.json` is a declared route in their manifest (`wellKnownInterlace` kind), synthesized by `listActorCaBundleEpochs` from their `actor_ca_bundle` table, which already carries epoch, signing_key_pubkey_b64u, cert_der_b64u, issued_at_ms, retired_at_ms, status, compromise_notice_b64u and external_anchor_uri — the RECEIPTS.md §2.3 shape. Nothing to build there.

notme's half — retaining retired keys so they remain resolvable — landed in PR #64: the `retired_keys` table, written BEFORE the DELETE in rotate() (signing-authority.ts:1122 / :1130), plus getEpochPublicKey().

THE GAP: cloister populates its archive from what it OBSERVES, polling notme's /internal/ca-bundle (which publishes current + prev key only). If cloister misses an epoch — it wasn't running, or notme rotated twice between polls — that epoch is absent from cloister's archive permanently. notme HAS the key in retired_keys, but there is no way to hand it over: `ReceiptSigner` exposes only `receiptFacts` and `signReceipt`, pinned by rpc-surface.do.test.ts.

So the failure mode this bead closes is narrow but real: a receipt naming epoch N is unverifiable not because the key was destroyed (fixed) but because the only party publishing it never saw it.

FIX: expose it on the entrypoint —

    async epochPublicKey(epoch: number):
      Promise<{ ok: true; publicRawB64: string; kid: string; retiredAt: number | null }
             | { ok: false; code: "EPOCH_UNKNOWN"; message: string }>

Returning a union rather than null-or-throw, per ADR-016 rule 5. `EPOCH_UNKNOWN` must be honest: an auditor has to distinguish "notme does not have this" from a transport failure, and both currently look the same.

Then update rpc-surface.do.test.ts's ReceiptSigner allow-list — deliberately, in the same diff, because that test exists so a new RPC method cannot appear without someone deciding it should.

Nothing about this is public-facing on notme's side: it is a service-binding RPC, and the data is public key material already published in the CA bundle.

Related: notme-acd503 (the retention half, landed), notme-c1b7fd (receipt signing).
acceptance_criteria: `ReceiptSigner.epochPublicKey(epoch)` returns a result union resolving any epoch present in retired_keys or the current one, with EPOCH_UNKNOWN distinguishable from failure. rpc-surface.do.test.ts's allow-list updated in the same change. `task worker:check` green.

comments.text:
Committed as 5bfcd63 on main.

**Security review additions over the initial draft:**
1. Socket file chmod'd to 0600 right after bind. The bridge cert means anyone with `connect()` access can fetch as the bridge identity — owner-only is the right default for the local-trust model from the parent epic. There's a microsecond chmod-after-bind race window; mitigated by directory perms (operator concern). A future hardening could set umask before bind for a tighter guarantee, but that needs a libc dep so it's out of scope here.

title: red-team:replay — receipt epoch is unresolvable after two rotations; A can repudiate every receipt it ever signed
description:
Filed from adversarial review of PR #61 (branch notme-c1b7fd-receipt-signing), protocol-replay/epoch-confusion lens.

## Location
- worker/src/signing-authority.ts:822 `rotate()`
- worker/src/signing-authority.ts:768 `generateBundle()`
- worker/src/signing-authority.ts:492 `getReceiptFacts()`
- Spec: cloister interlace-spec/0.2.0-draft/RECEIPTS.md §2.2.2 step 2, §2.3

## Captured message
Any signed Interlace receipt, i.e. `Ed25519_Sign(master_sk_N, commitment_cbor)` where the commitment names `epoch: N` and `actor_fp: SHA-256(pub_N)`.

## The defect
RECEIPTS.md §2.2.2 (V historical audit) requires the auditor to resolve the pubkey for the receipt's *named epoch* from an archival CA bundle, at arbitrary later time T. §2.3 makes this MUST: "Historical pubkeys remain resolvable by epoch number until A's CA bundle is decommissioned entirely... without that, A can defeat audits by aggressive key rotation."

notme cannot satisfy this today, and PR #61 does not add it:

1. `rotate()` executes `DELETE FROM keys WHERE id = 'authority'` — the epoch-N keypair is destroyed.
2. It then writes `prevKeyId` / `prevPubKey` into DO storage. Single slot, unconditionally overwritten on the next rotation. Depth = 1.
3. `generateBundle()` publishes `{ epoch, seqno, keys: {curKeyId: pub, prevKeyId: prevPub}, keyId, prevKeyId }`. `keys` is keyed by **keyId**, not by epoch. The bundle carries exactly one `epoch` field (the current one). There is no epoch → pubkey mapping for any historical epoch, and no `.well-known/interlace/index.json` exists in notme at all (the well-known routes are jwks.json, signet-authority.json, ca-bundle.pem, oauth-authorization-server, openid-configuration, security.txt).

Consequence: after the second `rotate()`, `pub_N` exists nowhere. Every receipt naming epoch N fails §2.2.2 step 2 permanently.

## Resulting state
A (notme+cloister) can void the evidentiary weight of every receipt it has ever issued with two administrative actions. §2.5 says a valid receipt plus absence of `nonce(r)` from D_A proves off-record admission. A receipt whose epoch pubkey cannot be resolved is not a valid receipt, so the §2.5 / §13.2 claim collapses to nothing. This is precisely the repudiation the receipt exists to prevent, and the adversary in a non-repudiation system *is* A.

The existing model actively fights this: worker/src/revocation.ts:55 defines `epoch_mismatch // token.epoch < bundle.epoch` as a *revocation reason*, and :364 rejects any keyId not equal to `bundle.keyId` or `bundle.prevKeyId`. notme's key lifecycle is built on "old epoch = dead", which is right for 10-minute access tokens and wrong for permanent evidence. PR #61 introduces the first artifact whose verifiability must outlive rotation, and reuses the token retention policy unchanged.

## Detection difficulty
A third-party auditor cannot distinguish "A rotated twice and lost the key" from "this receipt was forged" from "A is stonewalling". Both present as an unresolvable epoch. Silence is not evidence here — it is indistinguishable from data loss, which §2.3's lost-bundle-recovery section explicitly tries to close via `external_anchor_uri`.

## Closing playbook
1. Add a `retired_keys(epoch INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, key_id TEXT, public_raw_b64 TEXT, retired_at INTEGER)` table; `rotate()` inserts the outgoing (epoch, keyId, pubkey) *before* the DELETE. Never prune.
2. Serve `/.well-known/interlace/index.json` per §2.3: every epoch entry with `status: "active" | "retired"`, retirement timestamp, and a published `ca_decommission_after`.
3. Key the receipt-verification lookup by **epoch**, not keyId. The bundle's `keys` map cannot answer "pubkey for epoch N".
4. §2.3(1): publish each per-epoch pubkey to an independent append-only anchor at mint time (`external_anchor_uri`) so a notme data-loss event does not silently look like a successful repudiation.
5. ADR-014 should state the retention obligation explicitly — it currently mentions retired epochs only at line 112, as a reason to derive `epoch`, and says nothing about keeping the key resolvable.

## Severity
BLOCKER / HIGH. Confidence 8/10 on the mechanism (verified in code); the adversary is the operator, which is the correct threat model for non-repudiation.
acceptance_criteria: A test in worker/src/signing-authority.do.test.ts that rotates twice and then resolves the pubkey for the original epoch from the published bundle/well-known surface, and succeeds. Run: `cd worker && pnpm vitest run src/signing-authority.do.test.ts`.

title: red-team:replay — timestamp_ms is unbounded, letting a compromised binding holder backdate fabricated receipts arbitrarily
description:
Filed from adversarial review of PR #61 (branch notme-c1b7fd-receipt-signing), protocol-replay/evidence-forgery lens.

## Location
worker/src/receipts/commitment.ts:193 — `const timestampMs = requireUint(decoded, "timestamp_ms");` and nothing else. Any non-negative safe integer is accepted (0 .. 9_007_199_254_740_991 ms, i.e. 1970 .. year 287396).

## Captured message / attacker position
Anything holding the `ReceiptSigner` service binding: a compromised cloister deployment, a compromised Worker in the same account, or a supply-chain compromise of cloister's build.

## Why this is in-scope rather than "the design trusts the binding holder"
ADR-014's own premise is that cloister holding `RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY` in its env is unsafe and the key belongs in notme. If the binding holder were trusted absolutely, moving the key buys nothing. The PR clearly agrees — it bounds the compromise on several axes:
- cross-format forgery: blocked (parse + canonical re-encode + byte equality)
- `actor_fp`: derived, not received
- `epoch`: derived, not received
- `status`: pinned to 2xx, with the explicit stated reason "Signing one for a 4xx/5xx would let a caller manufacture evidence that a request it never served succeeded" (commitment.ts:186-188)

`timestamp_ms` is the one remaining field that is (a) fully attacker-chosen, (b) semantically load-bearing, and (c) cheaply boundable by notme — and it is unbounded. `nonce`, `request_hash`, `body_hash`, `headers_hash` are correctly left unvalidated because notme structurally cannot see the request; `timestamp_ms` has no such excuse, notme has a clock.

## Concrete exploit
A compromised binding holder mints N receipts with attacker-chosen `nonce`, `request_hash`, `body_hash`, `headers_hash`, `status: 200`, and `timestamp_ms` spread across the last two years. Each is a valid Ed25519 signature under A's master key over a canonical commitment. Under §2.5, each one whose nonce is absent from D_A is proof that A admitted a request off-record. A cannot disprove any of them — the signature is A's own.

The spec's live clock check does not help. §2.2.1 step 12 bounds `timestamp_ms` to ±300s of **P's** clock, and §2.2.2 audit reuses that step. The attacker is the party supplying both the receipt and the claimed request, so it simply asserts a matching request time. Only notme-side clamping constrains the value.

With clamping, the same compromise yields receipts that can only be dated to the window in which the attacker actually held the binding — bounded, correlatable with notme's own access records, and impossible to backfill into a fabricated history.

## Detection difficulty
An offline auditor holding the master pubkey sees a perfectly valid receipt. There is nothing in the signed bytes that distinguishes a backdated fabrication from a genuine two-year-old admission.

## Closing playbook
In `validateCommitment`, after `requireUint`:

```
const now = Date.now();
if (timestampMs < now - RECEIPT_CLOCK_SKEW_MS || timestampMs > now + RECEIPT_CLOCK_SKEW_MS) {
  fail("TIMESTAMP_OUT_OF_WINDOW", ...);
}
```

Pass `nowMs` in via `CommitmentFacts` (alongside `actorFp` / `epoch`) so it stays derived-not-received and remains testable. 300_000 ms matches RECEIPTS.md §2.2.1 step 12 and 0.1.0 §6.2.7, so the clamp is spec-justified and cannot reject a receipt a conformant P would have accepted. Both notme and cloister run on Cloudflare's clock, so real skew is sub-second.

Also document the residual in ADR-014: even clamped, a compromised binding holder can fabricate `nonce` / `request_hash` / `body_hash` / `headers_hash` freely. That is structurally unboundable and should be stated, not left implicit.

## Severity
MEDIUM. Confidence 8/10.
acceptance_criteria: Tests in worker/src/__tests__/receipt-commitment.test.ts assert rejection of a commitment with timestamp_ms far in the past (e.g. 0) and far in the future, and acceptance within the tolerance window. Run: `cd worker && pnpm vitest run src/__tests__/receipt-commitment.test.ts`.

title: cert-authority.ts + signing-authority.ts + token.ts — Ed25519 as any casts are a WebCrypto TS lib gap, document it
description:
Multiple security-critical crypto call sites use `{ name: "Ed25519" } as any` or `"Ed25519" as any` to work around a missing Ed25519 entry in the TypeScript DOM lib's `SubtleCrypto` overloads:

- `worker/src/cert-authority.ts`: lines 48, 65, 115
- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts`: lines 126, 136, 155, 192, 279, 311, 423
- `worker/src/auth/token.ts`: lines 78, 113

These `as any` casts suppress type-checking on the algorithm parameter passed to `crypto.subtle.generateKey/importKey/sign/verify`. If the string is wrong (e.g., typo or wrong casing), the runtime throws but TS doesn't catch it at compile time.

The casts are structurally necessary given the current `@cloudflare/workers-types` lib — Ed25519 was added to the spec but typings lag. However they are undocumented, making them look like lazy workarounds.

Fix options:
1. Add a top-of-file comment in each affected file explaining the cast is a DOM lib gap, not a type escape hatch. (docs)
2. Define a typed `const ED25519_ALGO = { name: "Ed25519" } as AlgorithmIdentifier` constant and use it throughout — narrows the surface of `as any` to one declaration. (tidy)

The `cert-exchange.ts:142` cast `(body.proof as any).type` in the exhaustive-check branch is a TypeScript narrowing artifact — correct but worth a comment.

title: notme: M1 — OIDC audience pin "notme.bot" incoherent for Google ID tokens
description:

- worker/worker.ts:1465 (/auth/oidc/login)
- worker/src/cert-exchange.ts:106

(a) These OIDC paths cannot accept Google tokens at all today (audience check always fails),
(b) The audience pin is wrong and should be the Google client ID from env, OR
(c) The OIDC paths are dead code that should be removed.

1. Remove the Google branch from TRUSTED_ISSUERS until the audience plumbing is right
2. Add per-issuer audience expectations: `Map<issuer, expected-audience>` keyed by env config (e.g. `OIDC_CLIENT_ID_GOOGLE`)

The structural fix landed in 5639328 (audience required at type level) is correct — this is just about the VALUE being pinned looking wrong for some issuers.

title: red-team:trust-root — validateCommitment signs float64 timestamp_ms: every receipt is non-canonical, every conformant commitment is rejected
description:
Filed from adversarial review of PR #61 (branch `notme-c1b7fd-receipt-signing`), trust-root lens.

## Location
- `worker/src/receipts/commitment.ts:20-26` (Encoder), `:36-42` (Decoder), `:118-126` (`requireUint`), `:229` (the equality check)

## Summary
The "canonically re-encode and require byte equality" gate — the single defense that makes signing with the CA master key safe — is pinned to **cbor-x's encoder behavior**, not to RFC 8949 §4.2. cbor-x diverges from §4.2 for integers >= 2^32, and `timestamp_ms` is unix **milliseconds**, so every real commitment crosses that boundary.

Empirically (cbor-x 1.6.4, the pinned version):
- `cbor.encode(1775000000000)` -> `fb4279d463e9600000` — CBOR **major type 7 float64**, not the shortest-form uint64 `1b0000019d463e9600`.
- `cborDecoder.decode(0x1b ...)` -> **BigInt**, which `requireUint` rejects (`typeof v !== "number"` -> `FIELD_NOT_UINT`).

## Proof (against the real module, esbuild-bundled and run under node)
Hand-built RFC 8949 §4.2 canonical commitment (what fxamacker/cbor `CanonicalEncOptions`, ciborium, or any conformant encoder emits):
```
...6c74696d657374616d705f6d73 1b0000019d463e9600
=> REJECTED: FIELD_NOT_UINT - "timestamp_ms" must be a non-negative CBOR integer
```
The form notme actually accepts and signs:
```
...6c74696d657374616d705f6d73 fb4279d463e9600000
=> ACCEPTED and SIGNED
```
Same 243-byte length, diverging at offset 234. All other seven fields encode canonically; only `timestamp_ms` is wrong.

## Why this is a trust-root defect, not just interop
`interlace-spec/0.2.0-draft/RECEIPTS.md` §2.1 types `timestamp_ms` as `<uint>` and requires `canonical_cbor()` = RFC 8949 §4.2 with "shortest length form for integers". §3.1 "canonicalization landmines" is explicit: **"Floats and NaN are forbidden... canonical receipt schemas in this spec contain no float fields at all... always use uint milliseconds rather than float seconds."** notme emits precisely the forbidden construct, and §3.1 also says conformant decoders MUST reject non-conformant encodings.

Consequences:
1. **The non-repudiation property the PR exists to establish does not hold.** §2.2.2 V-archival audit decodes `commitment_cbor` strictly; a float where a uint is specified fails. Receipts notme signs are not usable as evidence by an independent auditor — the entire point of moving the key into notme.
2. **The ADR's central claim is false.** `docs/design/014-receipt-signing.md`: "a receipt notme signed is canonically encoded, so a verifier recomputing the digest gets the same answer." It is guaranteed non-canonical.
3. **Fails closed for conformant callers.** A Go/Rust cloister emitting spec-canonical commitments gets `FIELD_NOT_UINT` on 100% of requests. The path only works because cloister also pins `cbor-x ^1.6.4` — cbor-x validated against itself.
4. **The signable byte set is defined by a caret-ranged third-party encoder.** What the CA master key will sign is `{b : cborX.encode(cborX.decode(b)) == b}`, not "canonical CBOR". A cbor-x minor bump that fixes this very bug silently changes the accepted set and makes every previously issued receipt unreproducible.

## Why the tests missed it
`worker/src/__tests__/receipt-commitment.test.ts` (17 passing) and `worker/src/receipt-signer.do.test.ts` both build fixtures with the same cbor-x Encoder they validate against, so the fixed point is trivially satisfied. RECEIPTS.md §7 requires `receipt-canonical-bytes.json` with "`timestamp_ms` near uint8/uint16/uint32 boundaries" — that pinned vector does not exist here and would have caught this immediately.

## Why `bundleCanonical` escaped
`worker/src/revocation.ts:250` feeds the same cbor-x Encoder and claims byte-parity with signet's `BundleCanonical`. It survives only because `issuedAt` is in **seconds** (~1.75e9 < 2^32, encoded `0x1a`), not milliseconds. So the comment in `commitment.ts:18-19` ("Encoder settings must match `bundleCanonical`") is false comfort: identical settings, different value ranges, different conformance outcome. That path breaks in 2106.

## Fix
Do not delegate the signing input to cbor-x's encoder. The schema is eight fixed fields — hand-roll the ~40-line RFC 8949 §4.2 encoder (definite-length map, shortest-form uint header, byte strings, text keys pre-sorted) so "what the CA master key will sign" is defined by the spec rather than by a dependency's incidental behavior. Correspondingly accept `number | bigint` in `requireUint` (cbor-x surfaces `0x1b` as BigInt) and normalize before the range checks. Then pin the RECEIPTS.md §7 `receipt-canonical-bytes.json` vector — including a `timestamp_ms` above 2^32 — as a cross-implementation contract test, the way `key-id.ts` pins its ADR-012 conformance vector.

## Confidence
High (9/10). Reproduced against the shipped module; spec text is explicit and normative.

## Reproduction
Bundle the module and run the two-arm PoC:
```
cd worker && ./node_modules/.bin/esbuild src/receipts/commitment.ts --bundle --format=esm --platform=node --outfile=/tmp/commitment.mjs
# then call validateCommitment with a hand-built 0x1b-form commitment (rejected)
# and with cbor.encode(map) (accepted, 0xfb float64 tail)
```

comments.text:
CLOSING — both halves fixed and verified against merged main, including the re-encode half cloister could not confirm from outside.

DECODE HALF (the one cloister could see): `requireUint` accepts bigint. cbor-x decodes a shortest-form uint64 to BigInt, and the old `typeof v !== "number"` guard therefore rejected 100% of commitments from any spec-conformant encoder.

RE-ENCODE HALF (the one they asked about): cbor-x is no longer used for encoding at all. `commitment.ts:21` imports `encodeCanonicalMap` from a hand-rolled RFC 8949 §4.2 encoder (worker/src/receipts/canonical-cbor.ts), and `:319` uses it for the re-encode. `grep -n Encoder worker/src/receipts/commitment.ts` returns nothing — the module imports `Decoder` only. cbor-x cannot emit a float64 into the signing input because it no longer emits the signing input.

Proved rather than reasoned, running the merged encoder:

    ts 4294967295     head 70   (uint32)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false
    ts 4294967296     head 1b   (uint64)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false
    ts 1775000000000  head 1b   (uint64)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false
    ts <now>          head 1b   (uint64)  contains /fb[0-9a-f]{16}/: false

Exactly at and across the 2^32 boundary, which is where the bug lived.

WHY THE HAND-ROLL RATHER THAN A CBOR-X FLAG: what the CA master key signs should be defined by the spec, not by a dependency's incidental behaviour. Under the old arrangement a cbor-x minor bump fixing this very bug would silently change the signable byte set and make every prior receipt unreproducible.

THE JOINT VECTOR IS THE RIGHT THING TO KEEP ASKING ABOUT, and cloister is right that it is what catches this on both sides. notme pins the same 12 cases at worker/src/__tests__/vectors/receipt-canonical-bytes.json, generated by encoding each input with BOTH cloister's canonicalCbor(commitmentCborMap(...)) and notme's encodeCanonicalMap(...) and requiring byte-for-byte agreement — 0 disagreements across all 12. Cloister asserts no float64 heads via not.toMatch(/fb[0-9a-f]{16}/); notme asserts the same property as not.toContain(0xfb) plus a full byte-equality check per vector.

The reason this bug shipped with 17 green tests is worth keeping attached to the closure: every fixture was built with the same encoder being validated, which is a fixed point rather than a conformance check — any self-consistent encoder passes it, including a wrong one. It was found by running cloister's real output through notme's validator. The joint vector exists so that is a standing check rather than a one-off.

title: P0: TS adopts canonical CBOR for CABundle signing canonicalization (per ADR-010 + signet protocol)
description:
Implements `docs/design/010-cross-language-canonical-encoding.md`.

## Scope

ONLY the cryptographic canonical bytes (Ed25519 sign/verify input). JSON stays load-bearing for everything else (HTTP API, KV storage, DO blob columns, DPoP/JWT) — that matches signet's own architecture.

## What changes

1. Add `cbor-x` to `worker/package.json` (Workers V8 compatible, RFC 8949 §4.2 deterministic encoding).
2. Replace `worker/src/revocation.ts::bundleCanonical()` body with CBOR-canonical encoding using integer-keyed map matching signet exactly:
   ```
   1 → Epoch     (uint64)
   2 → Seqno     (uint64)
   3 → Keys      (map[string][]byte)
   4 → KeyID     (string)
   5 → PrevKeyID (string, "" if absent)
   6 → IssuedAt  (int64)
   ```
3. Replace inline duplicate at `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:443-447` with import of the shared `bundleCanonical()` function (closes companion bead notme-XXX P3 dedupe).
4. Cross-runtime fixture suite at `schema/fixtures/cabundle-*.bin` + `*.expected.hex` — signet Go produces fixture; notme TS asserts byte-equality.
5. Migration: dual-encode for one rotation cycle (writer signs both JSON-canonical and CBOR-canonical, verifier accepts either), then drop JSON.

## Acceptance

- `bundleCanonical()` output for a known-fixture bundle byte-equals signet's `encMode.Marshal(message)` output.
- All existing tests pass (`npx vitest run`).
- New cross-runtime fixture test asserts byte equality.
- Schema docstring matches reality.

## Verification ladder

1. `npx tsc --noEmit` clean.
2. `npx vitest run` 332/332 + new fixture test.
3. Manual: take a notme-issued bundle, run signet Go's verifier against it. Should succeed.
4. Manual: take a signet Go-issued bundle, run notme TS verifier against it. Should succeed.

## Anchors

- `docs/design/010-cross-language-canonical-encoding.md` — the decision.
- `signet/pkg/revocation/checker.go:168-188` — byte-for-byte target.
- `signet/pkg/revocation/cabundle/https_fetcher.go` — confirms JSON is transport, CBOR is signing-only.
- `worker/src/revocation.ts:159-166` — function to replace.
- `worker/src/signing-authority.ts:443-447` — inline duplicate to remove.
- `schema/identity.capnp` — already updated (docstring fix landed with ADR-010).

title: P1: schema sync drift — capnp-to-ts.ts silently degrades on unknown features
description:
Independent of wire-format work (`docs/design/010-...`). This is type-sync correctness, not signature canonicalization.

## The hole

`schema/codegen/capnp-to-ts.ts` is a 280-LOC hand-rolled regex parser. It silently drops:

- `Float*` types (no Float32, Float64)
- Smaller-than-32 ints (no Int8, UInt8, Int16, UInt16)
- `AnyPointer`
- Annotations (e.g. workerd-style `$compatEnableDate`)
- Groups
- Generics
- Interfaces

When unknown features appear in `schema/identity.capnp`, the generator falls through to `unknown` / `z.unknown()` rather than erroring. A future schema edit that uses any of these can ship without anyone noticing — runtime Zod validation passes whatever, downstream code thinks it has type safety it doesn't.

## Two fix options

**(A) Replace with proper capnp toolchain.**
- `capnp-ts` library (npm). Real capnp wire format support.
- May or may not work on Workers V8; needs vetting.
- Heaviest. Fully fixes the silent-degradation problem AND opens the door to using real capnp wire format if ever desired (we explicitly chose CBOR per ADR-010, so this isn't load-bearing — but parity with the Go-side `capnpc-go` output becomes possible).

**(B) Fail-loud-on-unknown-features.**
- Keep `capnp-to-ts.ts` simple but add an exhaustive switch on capnp types.
- Unknown features throw at codegen time with a helpful error message ("AnyPointer not supported by capnp-to-ts.ts; consider option A or rewrite the schema").
- Cheaper. Doesn't fix the underlying limitation; just makes drift impossible.

Most likely the right answer is (B) for now (cheap, immediately stops drift), with a follow-up bead for (A) if the schema ever needs features (B) doesn't support.

## Acceptance

- (A): `gen/ts/identity.ts` is byte-equal output of a real capnp toolchain run; CI runs the codegen + asserts no drift; capnp toolchain version pinned.
- (B): adding a `Float64` field to `schema/identity.capnp` and running `task schema:ts` errors out with a clear message; exhaustive type list in the generator's switch is documented as the supported subset.

## Anchors

- `schema/codegen/capnp-to-ts.ts` — the parser.
- `schema/identity.capnp` — the source.
- `gen/ts/identity.ts` — the output.
- `ley-line-open/docs/decades/T8/capnp-rtfm-findings.md` — capnp tooling research.

Replaces part of `notme-803923` (the schema-sync portion).

title: Reshape mintBridgeCertPair into /identity/lease — {scope, peer} mint endpoint
description:
Per cloister ADR-0006 draft (cloister-bc8b0f). REVISED — the master CA + cert minting are already shipped; this is a reshape, not a new build.

The notme worker already has:
- `SigningAuthority` DO — Ed25519 master CA, key born-in-CF, never leaves
- `cert-authority.ts::mintBridgeCertPair` — mints 5-min ephemeral P-256 cert pair (mTLS + signing) signed by Ed25519 master, with X.509 KeyUsage + EKU + custom-OID extensions
- `cert-exchange.ts::handleCertExchange` — endpoint shape that takes a proof and returns a cert pair
- `revocation.ts` — epoch-bundle CA rotation

The Interlace lease shape is a narrower variant of `mintBridgeCertPair`: single signing cert, scoped, peer-bound.

## Endpoint
`POST /identity/lease`
Request:
```json
{ "scope": "bead_create:/repos/rosary", "peer": "sha256:...", "ttl_seconds": 300 }
```
Response: ephemeral signing cert (DER) + ephemeral private key. Same wire shape as the signing half of `mintBridgeCertPair`.

## Auth on the mint
Caller authenticates with an existing notme proof (DPoP / OIDC token via `auth/verify-proof.ts` — already shipped). The mint endpoint does NOT require a Signet cert (chicken-and-egg).

## Cert extensions to add
- Existing custom-OID arc (`1.3.6.1.4.1.99999`) already used by `mintBridgeCertPair` — extend with:
  - `interlace-peer` (peer fingerprint from request)
  - `interlace-scope` (scope from request, opaque string)
- Reuse the same DER encoding helpers in `cert-authority.ts`.

## Scope grammar
Opaque to notme — caller-supplied string, signed verbatim. Cloister parses + checks. Optional notme-side allowlist policy if desired (env-configurable list of permitted scope prefixes per principal).

## Success criteria
- ~50–100 LOC delta in worker — new route + scope-grammar wrapper around existing mint.
- Round-trip test: `POST /identity/lease` → verify with leyline-sign WASM (per ley-line-* sibling) → cert chains to master, scope present, TTL bounded.
- No changes to `SigningAuthority` DO. No new master keys. No new revocation primitives.

## Out of scope
- Revocation broadcast (open Q from ADR-0006 — separate bead).
- Multi-master / federation.

title: notme: add /internal/sign-receipt endpoint (production receipts emission path)
description:
## What

Cross-repo bead. Add `/internal/sign-receipt` to notme's worker so cloister can delegate Interlace 0.2.0 receipt signing to notme instead of holding the receipt signing key in cloister's env.

## Why

Per cloister's receipts impl (`cloister-ae713f`, shipped 2026-05-12): the TS implementation today reads `RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY` env binding directly. Production deployments should delegate to notme for the same key-isolation rationale as JWT signing — notme holds the actor's master signing key in `SigningAuthority` DO; cloister never sees raw bytes.

The receipts agent's `loadReceiptSigner()` in `src/routes/receipt-emitter.ts` already has a TODO stub for this: "when this binding is unset and `env.NOTME` is configured, the receipt emitter forwards to notme's `/internal/sign-receipt` endpoint."

## Scope (notme-side)

New endpoint on `notme/worker/worker.ts`:

```
POST /internal/sign-receipt
Body: { "commitment_bytes_b64": "...", "actor_fp": "..." }
Response: { "signature_b64": "...", "epoch": 3 }
```

Backed by `SigningAuthority.signReceipt(commitment_bytes)` in `notme/worker/src/signing-authority.ts`. Same crypto primitives the existing JWT signing path uses (Ed25519 over canonical bytes).

## Constraints

- Endpoint is `/internal/*` — accessible only via service binding from cloister, NOT public
- Verify caller is cloister-router via the existing intra-platform unforgeability of the service binding
- Returns the current epoch alongside the signature (so cloister can populate the receipt's `epoch` field)
- Must work with the existing notme key-rotation cadence (alarm-driven, 4-min refresh)

## Coordinated with

- `cloister-ae713f` (shipped) — defines the wire shape this endpoint serves
- ADR-0018 future work — when notme co-locates as `notme-identity` bundle in cloister-router, this endpoint moves in-process (still same shape)

## Done when

- Endpoint exists in notme/worker; tests cover happy path + error cases
- Cloister's `loadReceiptSigner` migrates from env-direct to notme-delegated when `env.NOTME` is bound
- The intra-platform binding security boundary is preserved (no public access)

comments.text:
FROM CLOISTER — receipt migration LANDED. c00e923 on cloister's `integration` branch. task lint green (105 files / 1597 tests), lint:binding-parity clean. You were right to leave this open; the JWT commit did not cover it.

ALL FOUR STEPS, as specified:
  1. NOTME_RECEIPTS as its OWN binding, entrypoint="ReceiptSigner" — not pinned onto NOTME. Your source comment about the earlier draft that would have broken the first integrator was read and heeded.
  2. receiptFacts() supplies actor_fp + epoch; cloister derives neither locally.
  3. signReceipt(canonicalCbor(commitment)).
  4. Branch on the code union; EPOCH_MISMATCH retries exactly ONCE, then throws.

TWO THINGS YOU MAY WANT TO CHECK, because they are choices rather than transcription:

(a) The retry rebuilds and re-encodes rather than re-sending. `epoch` is a field inside the commitment, so it is inside the signed bytes — a bare re-send would earn an identical rejection. Consequently cloister's signer returns the commitment it ACTUALLY signed, and the envelope is built from THAT. Building it from the caller's original would pair a stale commitment with a signature over a different one: a receipt that fails verification everywhere and explains itself nowhere. If your validator ever starts distinguishing 'epoch stale' from 'epoch never matched', that behaviour is what it will see.

(b) Your 240s suggestion is taken, as a SEPARATE constant. RECEIPT_EMIT_MAX_AGE_MS=240_000 governs emission; RECEIPT_CLOCK_SKEW_MS stays at the spec's 300_000 because that is the VERIFY tolerance applied to receipts cloister RECEIVES, and narrowing it would start rejecting conformant peers. Your reasoning about round-trip headroom applies only to the side that builds. Worth stating plainly since 'use 240s' could easily have been implemented as one constant and quietly broken inbound verification.

ONE FINDING FROM YOUR SIDE OF THE BOUNDARY, offered because it will bite the next integrator too. Cloister first detected a misconfigured binding by shape: typeof binding.signReceipt === 'function', to catch a plain binding resolving to your DEFAULT fetch handler — the exact hazard your comment warns about. Unit tests passed. The integration suite failed, because workerd RPC stubs are PROXIES: property access synthesizes a callable for any name, so the check passes for a fetch-only binding, a wrong entrypoint, and a typo alike. It reads like a guard and asserts nothing.

There is no synchronous way to tell a correct binding from a wrong one. Cloister now probes: call receiptFacts() and require the shape only the real entrypoint produces (32-byte actorFp, integer epoch). Cached, one round-trip per isolate, not cached on failure. If your integration note ever tells someone to 'check the binding is right', that is the only check that works — and it is worth saying, because the wrong one looks correct and passes its own tests.

Cloister's env path (RECEIPT_SIGNING_KEY) remains for tests and Phase-1 local dev only; the binding wins whenever it is present and probes clean, and a bound-but-unusable binding logs rather than silently falling back.

title: worker/src/revocation.test.ts is dead — uses cloudflare:test but vitest config doesn't include the file or configure the pool
description:
Discovered 2026-05-09 during ADR-010 implementation work.

## The hole

`worker/src/revocation.test.ts` exists, imports `cloudflare:test` (`env, runInDurableObject`), and contains tests for `bundleCanonical`, `verifyBundleSignature`, `RevocationAuthority` DO, and `checkRevocation`.

**It has not been running.** Two reasons:

1. **Path mismatch:** `vitest.config.ts` only includes `src/__tests__/**/*.test.ts`. The file is at `src/revocation.test.ts` (NOT under `__tests__/`).
2. **Pool not configured:** even if the path matched, `cloudflare:test` requires `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` configured as the test pool. The pool is in `package.json` devDeps but not wired into `vitest.config.ts`.

Result: full vitest run reports `Test Files 22 passed (22) Tests 332 passed (332)`, with revocation tests counted as zero.

## Why this matters

Every revocation test has been silently uncounted since the file was committed. Anyone working on `bundleCanonical`, `verifyBundleSignature`, the `RevocationAuthority` DO, or `checkRevocation` has been editing without test-suite signal.

This bead's discovery: while implementing ADR-010 (CBOR canonical encoding), I changed `bundleCanonical` from JSON-canonical to CBOR-canonical. The existing tests in `revocation.test.ts` (like "excludes signature field" using `TextDecoder.decode().toContain('signature')`) would have FAILED under CBOR (binary output, ASCII string match meaningless). They didn't fail because they didn't run.

Workaround already applied: ported the CBOR-canonical-relevant tests into a new `src/__tests__/bundle-canonical.test.ts` (pure-function tests, no DO dependency, runs under standard vitest config). The DO tests in `revocation.test.ts` remain dead.

## Two fix paths

**(A) Configure the workers pool** so `cloudflare:test` works.
- Update `vitest.config.ts` to use `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers` for the relevant include path.
- May require a separate `vitest.workers.config.ts` since pool-workers is its own runtime (different from the standard vitest pool used by other tests).
- Requires `wrangler.toml` referenced by the pool config.
- Once wired: revocation.test.ts can be moved to `src/__tests__/` and runs with full DO support.

**(B) Rewrite revocation.test.ts to not need cloudflare:test.**
- Inject DO state via mock interfaces; test logic without real DO bindings.
- Faster, simpler — but loses DO-runtime fidelity. May miss issues that only surface under real workerd.

(A) is the architecturally correct answer. (B) is the pragmatic short-term fix.

## Acceptance

- All revocation tests run under `npx vitest run`.
- `bundleCanonical`, `verifyBundleSignature`, `RevocationAuthority`, `checkRevocation` are exercised in CI.
- Net test count goes up by N (whatever revocation.test.ts contains).

## Anchors

- `worker/src/revocation.test.ts` — the dead file
- `worker/vitest.config.ts` — current config (excludes src/*.test.ts)
- `worker/package.json` — has `@cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers ^0.13.5` already
- `worker/src/__tests__/bundle-canonical.test.ts` — new pure-function tests (workaround)

title: notme: explore workerd-as-rope — content-addressed isolate composition
description:
Architectural sketch filed at `docs/design/010-workerd-as-rope.md` (NOT pushed yet — sitting on local main).

**Thesis.** A Worker deployment today is a config (one main script + bindings + wrangler.toml). Replace with: a deployment is a tree of content-addressed chunks; each chunk is a v8 isolate config or a Rust capability; the tree-root hash IS the deployment. workerd is one realization of a tree; Rust runtime walks the rope.

**Why it matters here.** It dissolves the "rename notme-proxy / extract a crate / two binaries" question — those are paradigm-internal to "binaries are durable." In CAS, chunks are durable, binaries are derived. notme-mtls-injector becomes a chunk-hash, not a binary.

**What it buys.**
- Dedup is automatic — same auth chunk used by N tenants stored once
- Versioning is structural — every deployment is a hash, diff is tree-diff, rollback is older root
- Distribution is git-semantics — pull root, walk tree, fetch missing chunks
- Capabilities are first-class chunks — splice in or out by hash
- "Worker name + account" stops being identity; content is identity

**What's underspecified (the real design work).**
1. Chunk schema (capnp? CBOR? v8-aware?)
2. Capability resolution (direct hash? interface + impl?)
3. State (where mutable lives — per-leaf DO-style? separate state-rope?)
4. Cross-deployment composition (share isolate? share chunk-on-disk?)
5. Identity at the rope level (root only, or every subtree?)
